--!nonstrict
local IS_ROBLOX = game ~= nil

local Flux
local Compat
local Interact
local sert
local engine
local bridge: () -> () = nil :: any
if IS_ROBLOX then
	local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
	Flux = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Flux")) :: any
	Compat = require(ReplicatedStorage.Flux:WaitForChild("Compat")) :: any
	Interact = require(ReplicatedStorage.Flux:WaitForChild("Interact")) :: any
	sert = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("sert")) :: any
else
	-- Headless: a sert.env engine on Flux's own manual clock, handed to Compat before Flux loads (Responsive reads
	-- the services at module load). Its Instances, services and RunService stand in for the engine's; its game is
	-- never the global `game`, so Flux keeps its headless Compat and Clock paths.
	sert = require("@sert") :: any
	(require("@sert/engine/datatypes") :: any).installGlobals()
	local HeadlessClock = require("../../src/Clock") :: any
	Compat = require("../../src/Compat") :: any
	engine = sert.env.new({
		isClient = true,
		isStudio = true,
		strict = true,
		host = {
			clock = HeadlessClock.now,
			spawn = Compat.task.spawn,
			defer = HeadlessClock.defer,
			delay = HeadlessClock.delay,
			wait = HeadlessClock.wait,
			cancel = HeadlessClock.cancel,
		},
	})
	for _, key in
		{
			"typeof",
			"Color3",
			"UDim",
			"UDim2",
			"Vector2",
			"Vector3",
			"CFrame",
			"Rect",
			"NumberRange",
			"Font",
			"TweenInfo",
			"Enum",
			"ColorSequence",
			"ColorSequenceKeypoint",
			"NumberSequence",
			"NumberSequenceKeypoint",
		}
	do
		Compat[key] = sert.env[key]
	end
	Compat.Instance = engine.Instance
	Compat.services = engine.services
	-- The engine's RunService phases run in Flux's Heartbeat; Clock.reset drops subscribers, so env.reset re-bridges.
	function bridge()
		HeadlessClock.connect("Heartbeat", function(dt: number)
			engine:step(dt)
		end)
	end
	bridge()
	Flux = require("../../src") :: any
	Interact = require("../../src/Interact") :: any
end

local Clock = Flux.Clock

local env = {
	IS_ROBLOX = IS_ROBLOX,
	Flux = Flux,
	Compat = Compat,
	sert = sert,
	engine = engine,
	workspace = if IS_ROBLOX then workspace else engine.workspace,
	Instance = Compat.Instance,
	Color3 = Compat.Color3,
	UDim = Compat.UDim,
	UDim2 = Compat.UDim2,
	Vector2 = Compat.Vector2,
	ColorSequence = Compat.ColorSequence,
	NumberSequence = Compat.NumberSequence,
	Enum = Compat.Enum,
	task = Compat.task,
}

function env.settle()
	if IS_ROBLOX then
		task.wait()
	else
		Clock.drain()
	end
end

function env.frame(dt: number?)
	if IS_ROBLOX then
		game:GetService("RunService").Heartbeat:Wait()
	else
		Clock.step(dt or 1 / 60)
	end
end

function env.frames(done: () -> boolean, count: number?): boolean
	local limit = count or 60
	for _ = 1, limit do
		if done() then
			return true
		end
		env.frame()
	end
	return done()
end

function env.mountUi(parent: any, viewport: Vector2): (any, () -> ())
	if IS_ROBLOX then
		return parent, function() end
	end
	local prevViewport = engine.workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize
	engine:setViewport(viewport)
	local screen = engine.Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	screen.IgnoreGuiInset = true
	screen.Parent = engine.LocalPlayer.PlayerGui
	return screen, function()
		screen:Destroy()
		engine:setViewport(prevViewport)
	end
end

function env.expectSpacing(elements: { GuiObject }, axis: "X" | "Y", expectedGap: number, tolerance: number?)
	local rectOf = sert.roblox.Layout.geometry.rect
	local eps = tolerance or 1
	for i = 2, #elements do
		local prev = rectOf(elements[i - 1])
		local cur = rectOf(elements[i])
		local gap = if axis == "X" then cur.x - (prev.x + prev.w) else cur.y - (prev.y + prev.h)
		sert.near(gap, expectedGap, eps, `{elements[i - 1].Name} -> {elements[i].Name} {axis} spacing`)
	end
end

function env.warnings(fn: () -> ()): { string }
	assert(type(fn) == "function", "env.warnings expects a function")
	local messages = {}
	Compat.setWarnHook(function(message: string)
		table.insert(messages, message)
	end)
	local ok, err = pcall(fn)
	Compat.setWarnHook(nil)
	if not ok then
		error(err, 0)
	end
	return messages
end

local freshCount = 0
function env.fresh(prefix: string): string
	freshCount += 1
	return `{prefix}{freshCount}`
end

function env.reset()
	if IS_ROBLOX then
		if Clock.isManual() then
			Clock.manual(false)
		end
	else
		if not Clock.isManual() then
			Clock.manual(true)
		else
			Clock.reset()
		end
		if engine ~= nil then
			bridge()
		end
	end
	Compat.setWarnHook(nil)
end

-- Probe helpers for global reactive state quiescence
function env.idle(targetFlux: any?, expectOpts: { contexts: { { context: any, default: any } }? }?): string?
	local F = targetFlux or Flux
	if F.getOwner() ~= nil then
		return "an owner leaked: Flux.getOwner() is not nil at top level"
	elseif F.isReactive() then
		return "a reaction leaked: Flux.isReactive() is true at top level"
	end
	F.retrack()
	if F.isReactive() then
		return "a suspended reaction leaked: Flux.retrack() at top level resumed tracking"
	elseif pcall(F.cleanup, function() end) then
		return "Flux.cleanup accepted a value at top level (an owner leaked)"
	end
	if expectOpts and expectOpts.contexts then
		for _, entry in expectOpts.contexts do
			local value = entry.context:get()
			if value ~= entry.default then
				return `a provided context leaked: it reads {value} at top level, expected its default {entry.default}`
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

function env.drained(targetFlux: any?): string?
	local F = targetFlux or Flux
	local runs = 0
	local probe = F.effect(function()
		runs += 1
	end)
	F.flush()
	local first = runs
	F.flush()
	probe:Destroy()
	if first ~= 1 then
		return `a fresh effect ran {first} times on flush, expected 1 (queue or flushing flag stuck)`
	elseif runs ~= first then
		return `a fresh effect ran again on a second flush ({runs - first} more runs)`
	end
	return nil
end

local defaultSnapshot: { [string]: { [string]: any } } = {}
for class, map in Flux.Defaults do
	defaultSnapshot[class] = table.clone(map)
end

local responsiveConfig = Flux.Responsive.config
local responsiveSnapshot: { [string]: any } = {}
for key, value in responsiveConfig do
	responsiveSnapshot[key] = if type(value) == "table" then table.clone(value) else value
end

local hooksInstalled = false
function env.installHooks()
	if hooksInstalled then
		return
	end
	hooksInstalled = true
	sert.afterEach(function()
		local leak = env.idle(Flux)
		Flux.Flags.defaults = true
		table.clear(Flux.Defaults)
		for class, map in defaultSnapshot do
			Flux.Defaults[class] = table.clone(map)
		end
		Interact._useHoverServices(nil)
		table.clear(responsiveConfig)
		for key, value in responsiveSnapshot do
			responsiveConfig[key] = if type(value) == "table" then table.clone(value) else value
		end
		Flux.Responsive.viewport:set(env.Vector2.new(1920, 1080))
		if engine ~= nil then
			engine:setViewport(env.Vector2.new(1920, 1080))
		end
		env.reset()
		assert(not leak, leak)
	end)
end

if IS_ROBLOX then
	env.installHooks()
end

return table.freeze(env)

-- Thief.luau — the shadow that patrols unlocked bases. A dark floating
-- orb with a red THIEF label: it glides to a base, takes the highest
-- occupied pedestal item, and drifts away.

local PartKit = require(script.Parent.Parent.Shared.PartKit)

local Thief = {}

local SPEED = 9

local function glide(model, from, to)
	local distance = (to - from).Magnitude
	local steps = math.max(1, math.floor(distance / (SPEED * 0.05)))
	for step = 1, steps do
		local alpha = step / steps
		local nextPos = from:Lerp(to, alpha)
		model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(nextPos))
		task.wait(0.05)
	end
end

local function buildThief(position)
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = "Thief"
	local body = PartKit.Ball(model, 2, position, Color3.fromRGB(25, 25, 35), Enum.Material.Neon)
	body.Name = "Shadow"
	body.Transparency = 0.25
	PartKit.Ball(model, 0.4, position + Vector3.new(-0.7, 0.5, 1.8), Color3.fromRGB(255, 40, 40), Enum.Material.Neon).Name = "EyeL"
	PartKit.Ball(model, 0.4, position + Vector3.new(0.7, 0.5, 1.8), Color3.fromRGB(255, 40, 40), Enum.Material.Neon).Name = "EyeR"
	PartKit.Label(body, "THIEF", Color3.fromRGB(255, 60, 60), 5)
	model.PrimaryPart = body
	model.Parent = workspace
	return model
end

-- target: { BaseCenter, Pedestals, IsLocked, OnStolen(index) }
-- Pedestals is an array of 8 entries, each a table or false.
function Thief.Run(target)
	task.spawn(function()
		local entry = Vector3.new(-130, 6, target.BaseCenter.Z + 30)
		local exitPoint = Vector3.new(130, 6, target.BaseCenter.Z - 30)
		local thief = buildThief(entry)
		local hover = target.BaseCenter + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)
		glide(thief, entry, hover)
		if target.IsLocked() then
			glide(thief, hover, exitPoint)
			thief:Destroy()
			return
		end
		local victim = 0
		for index = 1, #target.Pedestals do
			if target.Pedestals[index] then
				victim = index
			end
		end
		if victim > 0 then
			target.OnStolen(victim)
			task.wait(1)
		end
		glide(thief, hover, exitPoint)
		thief:Destroy()
	end)
end

return Thief

--!strict

-- Runs every check that CI runs in the same order
-- Usage (from repo root): lute run .lute/ci.luau
-- by @vuppyan

local fs = require("@std/fs")
local process = require("@std/process")

type Step = {
    name: string,
    args: { string },
}

-- ROBLOX type definitions are downloaded for the luau-lsp version pinned in
-- rokit.toml, so they always match the type checker
-- They are cached in .cache/ (gitignored) and only downloaded when the version
-- changes
local DEFINITIONS_FILE = "globalTypes.None.d.luau"
local CACHE_DIR = ".cache"

local function luauLspVersion(): string
    local rokit = fs.readFileToString("rokit.toml")
    local version = string.match(rokit, 'luau%-lsp%s*=%s*"[^"@]*@([^"]+)"')
    if version == nil then
        error("could not find luau-lsp version in rokit.toml", 0)
    end
    return version
end

local function ensureDefinitions(): string
    local version = luauLspVersion()
    local path = `{CACHE_DIR}/globalTypes-{version}.d.luau`
    if fs.exists(path) then
        return path
    end

    local url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JohnnyMorganz/luau-lsp/"
        .. `{version}/scripts/{DEFINITIONS_FILE}`
    print(`Downloading ROBLOX type definitions for luau-lsp {version}`)
    local result = process.run(
        { "curl", "-fsSL", "--create-dirs", "-o", path, url },
        { stdio = "inherit" }
    )
    if not result.ok then
        error(`Failed to download {url}`, 0)
    end
    return path
end

local definitions = ensureDefinitions()

-- `luau-lsp analyze` enables every Luau FFlag by default, but Studio and the
-- editor extension only enable released ones, so code that type checks with
-- the defaults can still show errors to users. Each typecheck step also runs
-- with `--no-flags-enabled` (plus the new solver) to match Studio
local STUDIO_FLAGS = "--no-flags-enabled"

-- `args` for a `luau-lsp analyze` step, with Studio's flags
local function withStudioFlags(args: { string }): { string }
    local result = table.clone(args)
    table.insert(result, 3, STUDIO_FLAGS)
    return result
end

local SRC_ARGS = {
    "luau-lsp",
    "analyze",
    "--platform=roblox",
    "--sourcemap=sourcemap.json",
    `--definitions={definitions}`,
    "--flag:LuauSolverV2=true",
    "src",
}

local TESTS_ARGS = {
    "luau-lsp",
    "analyze",
    "--platform=standard",
    "--flag:LuauSolverV2=true",
    "--ignore=src/**",
    "--ignore=tests/typing/**",
    "tests",
}

-- the branch being checked: the pull request's branch in CI, or the current
-- branch locally
local function currentBranch(): string?
    local branch = process.env.GITHUB_HEAD_REF
    if branch ~= nil and branch ~= "" then
        return branch
    end
    local result = process.run({ "git", "branch", "--show-current" })
    if not result.ok then
        return nil
    end
    return (string.gsub(result.stdout, "%s+$", ""))
end

-- on a release branch (release/vX.Y.Z), also checks that every file holds
-- X.Y.Z and that no [UNRELEASED] tags are left in src
local function versionArgs(): { string }
    local args = { "lute", "run", ".lute/version.luau" }
    local branch = currentBranch()
    local release = if branch ~= nil
        then string.match(branch, "^release/v?(%d+%.%d+%.%d+.*)$")
        else nil
    if release ~= nil then
        table.insert(args, release)
    end
    return args
end

-- Keep this list in sync with the CI section of CONTRIBUTING.md
-- CI runs this script, plus a separate docs job (moonwave build) that this
-- script does not cover
local STEPS: { Step } = {
    {
        name = "version",
        args = versionArgs(),
    },
    {
        name = "format",
        args = { "stylua", "--check", "src", "tests" },
    },
    {
        name = "docs format",
        args = { "lute", "run", ".lute/docs.luau", "--check" },
    },
    {
        name = "lint",
        args = { "selene", "src" },
    },
    {
        name = "sourcemap",
        args = {
            "rojo",
            "sourcemap",
            "default.project.json",
            "-o",
            "sourcemap.json",
        },
    },
    {
        -- src uses ROBLOX globals so it is checked
        -- against ROBLOX's type definitions
        name = "typecheck (src)",
        args = SRC_ARGS,
    },
    {
        name = "typecheck (src, Studio flags)",
        args = withStudioFlags(SRC_ARGS),
    },
    {
        -- tests run under Lute, so they are checked without ROBLOX globals
        -- src is ignored since it is checked above with ROBLOX globals, and
        -- would otherwise fail here on globals like task through requires
        -- tests/typing is ignored since it is checked by the next step, and
        -- some of its files are meant to fail
        name = "typecheck (tests)",
        args = TESTS_ARGS,
    },
    {
        name = "typecheck (tests, Studio flags)",
        args = withStudioFlags(TESTS_ARGS),
    },
    {
        -- the typing type functions only run at type-check time, so their
        -- tests are type checked, including cases that must fail
        name = "typecheck (typing)",
        args = { "lute", "run", ".lute/typing.luau" },
    },
    {
        name = "typecheck (typing, Studio flags)",
        args = { "lute", "run", ".lute/typing.luau", STUDIO_FLAGS },
    },
    {
        name = "test",
        args = { "lute", "test" },
    },
}

local failed: { string } = {}

for _, step in STEPS do
    print(`\n=== {step.name} ===`)
    local result = process.run(step.args, { stdio = "inherit" })
    if not result.ok then
        print(`--- {step.name} failed (exit code {result.exitcode})`)
        table.insert(failed, step.name)
    end
end

print("")
if #failed > 0 then
    print(`FAILED: {table.concat(failed, ", ")}`)
    process.exit(1)
end
print("All checks passed.")

--!strict
-- Bare-Luau compatibility smoke suite (runs directly under `luau` without sert mocks).

assert(
	game == nil
		and workspace == nil
		and Instance == nil
		and Enum == nil
		and Color3 == nil
		and Vector3 == nil
		and UDim == nil
		and UDim2 == nil
		and TweenInfo == nil
		and task == nil,
	"standalone smoke suite must run with zero Roblox globals"
)

local Flux = require("../src")

local function expectError(fn: () -> (), pattern: string, label: string)
	local ok, err = pcall(fn)
	assert(not ok and string.find(tostring(err), pattern, 1, true) ~= nil, `{label}: got {err}`)
end
local function callWith(fn: any, ...: any): () -> ()
	local args = { ... }
	return function()
		fn(table.unpack(args))
	end
end
local function ret(v: any)
	return function()
		return v
	end
end

-- Clock defaults to manual outside Roblox and supports opting into live mode.
local Clock, trace, waited = Flux.Clock, {}, false
assert(Clock.isManual() == true and type(Clock.now()) == "number" and type(Clock.wall()) == "number")
local disconnectHb = Clock.connect("Heartbeat", function(dt)
	table.insert(trace, `hb:{dt}`)
end)
Clock.delay(0.1, function()
	table.insert(trace, "delay")
end)
Clock.defer(function()
	table.insert(trace, "defer")
end)
coroutine.resume(coroutine.create(function()
	Clock.wait(0.05)
	waited = true
end))
Clock.drain()
Clock.step(0.1, 0.05)
assert(trace[1] == "defer" and waited and table.find(trace, "delay") ~= nil and table.find(trace, "hb:0.05") ~= nil)
disconnectHb()
Clock.reset()

Clock.manual(false)
local deferRanSync = false
Clock.defer(function()
	deferRanSync = true
end)
assert(not Clock.isManual() and deferRanSync and type(Clock.now()) == "number" and type(Clock.wall()) == "number")
expectError(callWith(Clock.connect, "Heartbeat", function() end), "requires Roblox RunService", "live connect")
expectError(callWith(Clock.delay, 0.01, function() end), "requires a task scheduler", "live delay")
expectError(callWith(Clock.wait, 0.01), "requires a task scheduler", "live wait")
Clock.manual(true)

-- Core reactive graph, stores, control flow, and async.
local cleanupScope = Flux.scope(function()
	local count, seen = Flux.signal(1), 0
	local doubled = Flux.computed(function()
		return count() * 2
	end)
	Flux.effect(function()
		seen = doubled()
	end)
	Flux.flush()
	assert(seen == 2)
	count(3)
	count(4)
	Flux.flush()
	assert(seen == 8 and doubled() == 8)

	local ctx = Flux.context("fallback")
	assert(ctx:get() == "fallback" and ctx:provide("scoped", function()
		return ctx:get()
	end) == "scoped")
	assert(Flux.safe(function(): string
		return error("boom")
	end, ret("off"))() == "off")

	local st = Flux.store({ items = { "a", "b" }, nested = { n = 10 } })
	local sum = Flux.computed(function()
		return st.nested.n + #st.items
	end)
	st.nested.n = 20
	assert(sum() == 22)

	local flag, arr = Flux.signal(true), Flux.signal({ "x", "y" })
	local shown = Flux.show(flag, ret("on"), ret("off"))
	local picked = Flux.switch(flag :: any)({ [true] = ret("ok") })
	local vals = Flux.forValue(arr, function(_i, v)
		return string.upper(v)
	end)
	local idxs = Flux.forIndex(arr, function(i, v)
		return `{i}={v}`
	end)
	local keys = Flux.forKey(arr, function(v)
		return v
	end, function(i, v)
		return `{v}:{i}`
	end)
	local sel = Flux.selector(Flux.signal("x"))
	Flux.flush()
	assert(
		shown() == "on"
			and picked() == "ok"
			and vals()[2] == "Y"
			and idxs()[2] == "2=y"
			and keys()[1] == "x:1"
			and sel("x")
	)
	flag(false)
	Flux.flush()
	local res = Flux.async(ret("ok"))
	Flux.flush()
	assert(shown() == "off" and picked() == nil and res.data() == "ok" and res.state() == "ready" and not res.loading())
end)
cleanupScope:Destroy()

-- Pure-Luau motion, Oklab vectors, and Responsive defaults.
local motionScope = Flux.scope(function()
	local nSpring = Flux.spring(0, 4, 1)
	nSpring(10)
	local vTween = Flux.tween(vector.create(0, 0, 0), { Time = 0.2, EasingStyle = "Linear" })
	vTween(vector.create(10, 20, 30))
	Clock.step(0.1)
	assert(nSpring() > 0 and vTween().x > 0 and vTween().x < 10)
	Clock.step(2)
	assert(math.abs(nSpring() - 10) < 1e-2 and math.abs(vTween().y - 20) < 1e-4)
end)
motionScope:Destroy()

local Oklab, lab: any = Flux.Color.Oklab, vector.create(0.5, 0.1, -0.05)
local lighter = Oklab.lighten(lab, 0.2)
assert(lighter.X > 0.69 and Oklab.saturate(lab, 0.1).Y ~= lab.Y and Oklab.rotateHue(lab, 90).Z ~= lab.Z)
assert(Oklab.grayscale(lab).Y == 0 and math.abs(Oklab.mix(lab, lighter, 0.5).X - 0.6) < 1e-5)
assert(Flux.Responsive.viewport:get().X == 1920 and Flux.Responsive.scale:get() == 1)
assert(Flux.Responsive.breakpoint:get() == "desktop" and type(Flux.Responsive.platform:get()) == "string")

-- Roblox-only boundaries fail fast outside Roblox.
expectError(function()
	Flux.new("Frame")({})
end, "requires a Roblox environment", "Flux.new")
expectError(function()
	Flux.edit({} :: any)({})
end, "requires a Roblox environment", "Flux.edit")
expectError(function()
	local _ = Flux.Sync.server
end, "Flux.Sync needs Roblox", "Flux.Sync.server")
expectError(function()
	local _ = Flux.Sync.client
end, "Flux.Sync needs Roblox", "Flux.Sync.client")
for _, name in
	string.split(
		"padding,corner,stroke,aspectRatio,list,grid,flex,scale,gradient,sizeConstraint,textSizeConstraint",
		","
	)
do
	expectError(callWith((Flux :: any)[name]), "requires a Roblox environment", `Flux.{name}`)
end
for _, name in string.split("pointIn,sunk,covered,hover,press,selected,focused", ",") do
	expectError(callWith((Flux.Interact :: any)[name]), "requires a Roblox environment", `Flux.Interact.{name}`)
end
local fakeColor: any = vector.create(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
for _, name in string.split("luminance,readable,contrast", ",") do
	expectError(callWith((Flux.Color :: any)[name], fakeColor, fakeColor), "Flux.Color requires Roblox Color3", name)
end
expectError(callWith(Flux.Color.lighten, fakeColor, 0.1), "Flux.Color requires Roblox Color3", "Color.lighten")
for _, name in string.split("fromLinear,toLinear", ",") do
	expectError(callWith((Flux.Color.sRGB :: any)[name], fakeColor), "Flux.Color requires Roblox Color3", `sRGB.{name}`)
	expectError(callWith((Oklab :: any)[name], lab), "Flux.Color requires Roblox Color3", `Oklab.{name}`)
end
expectError(callWith(Oklab.fromRGB, fakeColor), "Flux.Color requires Roblox Color3", "Oklab.fromRGB")
expectError(callWith(Oklab.toRGB, lab), "Flux.Color requires Roblox Color3", "Oklab.toRGB")
print("standalone ok")

-- World.luau — builds the floating market: water, docks, stalls, bases,
-- conveyor, lighthouse, lanterns, boats and palms, all from PartKit.

local Config = require(script.Parent.Parent.Shared.Config)
local PartKit = require(script.Parent.Parent.Shared.PartKit)

local World = {}

local WOOD = Color3.fromRGB(140, 95, 55)
local WOOD_DARK = Color3.fromRGB(105, 70, 40)
local TEAL = Color3.fromRGB(24, 150, 157)
local NEON_RED = Color3.fromRGB(255, 80, 50)
local NEON_CYAN = Color3.fromRGB(60, 220, 255)
local LEAF = Color3.fromRGB(50, 150, 70)
local TRUNK = Color3.fromRGB(110, 75, 40)
local ROOF_RED = Color3.fromRGB(180, 50, 45)

local function buildWater(folder)
	local water = PartKit.Box(folder, Config.WaterSize, Config.WaterPosition, TEAL, Enum.Material.Glass)
	water.Name = "Sea"
	water.Transparency = 0.25
end

local function buildDock(folder)
	PartKit.Box(folder, Config.DockSize, Config.DockPosition, WOOD, Enum.Material.WoodPlanks).Name = "MainDock"
	local bridges = {
		{ size = Vector3.new(10, 2, 40), pos = Vector3.new(-60, 0, -30) },
		{ size = Vector3.new(10, 2, 40), pos = Vector3.new(60, 0, -30) },
		{ size = Vector3.new(10, 2, 40), pos = Vector3.new(0, 0, 32) },
	}
	for i, bridge in ipairs(bridges) do
		local part = PartKit.Box(folder, bridge.size, bridge.pos, WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.WoodPlanks)
		part.Name = "Bridge" .. i
	end
	for x = -85, 85, 17 do
		PartKit.Cylinder(folder, 6, 1.2, Vector3.new(x, -2, -12), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood).Name = "Post"
		PartKit.Cylinder(folder, 6, 1.2, Vector3.new(x, -2, 12), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood).Name = "Post"
	end
end

local function buildStall(folder, position, index)
	local stall = Instance.new("Folder")
	stall.Name = "Stall" .. index
	stall.Parent = folder
	local counter = PartKit.Box(stall, Vector3.new(8, 3, 4), position + Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0), WOOD, Enum.Material.WoodPlanks)
	counter.Name = "Counter"
	PartKit.Cylinder(stall, 7, 0.6, position + Vector3.new(-3.5, 5, -1.5), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood).Name = "PostL"
	PartKit.Cylinder(stall, 7, 0.6, position + Vector3.new(3.5, 5, -1.5), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood).Name = "PostR"
	local roof = PartKit.Box(stall, Vector3.new(10, 0.6, 6), position + Vector3.new(0, 8, 0), ROOF_RED, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic)
	roof.Name = "Roof"
	local anchor = PartKit.Part(stall, {
		Name = "OfferAnchor",
		Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1),
		Position = position + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0),
		Transparency = 1,
		CanCollide = false,
	})
	return anchor
end

local function buildBase(folder, center, index)
	local base = Instance.new("Folder")
	base.Name = "Base" .. index
	base.Parent = folder
	local floor = PartKit.Box(base, Vector3.new(38, 2, 32), center, WOOD, Enum.Material.WoodPlanks)
	floor.Name = "Floor"
	local roof = PartKit.Box(base, Vector3.new(40, 1, 34), center + Vector3.new(0, 14, 0), ROOF_RED, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic)
	roof.Name = "Roof"
	for _, corner in ipairs({ Vector3.new(-18, 7, -15), Vector3.new(18, 7, -15), Vector3.new(-18, 7, 15), Vector3.new(18, 7, 15) }) do
		PartKit.Cylinder(base, 14, 0.8, center + corner, WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood).Name = "RoofPost"
	end
	local signPart = PartKit.Box(base, Vector3.new(10, 3, 0.6), center + Vector3.new(0, 11, -16), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.WoodPlanks)
	signPart.Name = "Sign"
	local signGui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
	signGui.Name = "SignGui"
	signGui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
	signGui.Parent = signPart
	local signText = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	signText.Name = "SignText"
	signText.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
	signText.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	signText.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
	signText.TextSize = 28
	signText.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 240, 200)
	signText.Text = "BASE " .. index
	signText.Parent = signGui
	local pedestals = {}
	local slot = 1
	for _, dz in ipairs({ -6, 6 }) do
		for _, dx in ipairs({ -12, -4, 4, 12 }) do
			local top = PartKit.Cylinder(base, 1, 4.5, center + Vector3.new(dx, 1.5, dz), Color3.fromRGB(200, 180, 140), Enum.Material.Marble)
			top.Name = "Pedestal" .. slot
			pedestals[slot] = center + Vector3.new(dx, 2, dz)
			slot += 1
		end
	end
	return {
		Folder = base,
		Center = center,
		Pedestals = pedestals,
		SignText = signText,
	}
end

local function buildConveyor(folder)
	local belt = PartKit.Box(folder, Vector3.new(130, 1, 8), Vector3.new(0, 0.5, 40), Color3.fromRGB(60, 60, 70), Enum.Material.Metal)
	belt.Name = "Conveyor"
	for x = -60, 60, 10 do
		local stripe = PartKit.Box(folder, Vector3.new(1.5, 0.2, 8), Vector3.new(x, 1.1, 40), NEON_CYAN, Enum.Material.Neon)
		stripe.Name = "Stripe"
	end
end

local function buildLighthouse(folder)
	local tower = PartKit.Cylinder(folder, 26, 8, Config.LighthousePosition + Vector3.new(0, 13, 0), Color3.fromRGB(240, 235, 220), Enum.Material.Concrete)
	tower.Name = "LighthouseTower"
	local beacon = PartKit.Ball(folder, 3, Config.LighthousePosition + Vector3.new(0, 28, 0), NEON_CYAN, Enum.Material.Neon)
	beacon.Name = "Beacon"
	local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
	light.Color = NEON_CYAN
	light.Range = 40
	light.Brightness = 2
	light.Parent = beacon
	local cap = PartKit.Cylinder(folder, 2, 10, Config.LighthousePosition + Vector3.new(0, 31, 0), ROOF_RED, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic)
	cap.Name = "LighthouseRoof"
end

local function buildLanterns(folder)
	for i = 1, 9 do
		local x = -80 + (i - 1) * 20
		local z = (i % 2 == 0) and -13 or 13
		local pole = PartKit.Cylinder(folder, 8, 0.5, Vector3.new(x, 4, z), WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood)
		pole.Name = "LanternPole" .. i
		local lamp = PartKit.Ball(folder, 1.2, Vector3.new(x, 8.5, z), NEON_RED, Enum.Material.Neon)
		lamp.Name = "Lantern" .. i
		local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
		light.Color = NEON_RED
		light.Range = 18
		light.Brightness = 1.5
		light.Parent = lamp
	end
end

local function buildBoats(folder)
	local spots = { Vector3.new(-100, -2, 40), Vector3.new(100, -2, -40), Vector3.new(40, -2, -90) }
	for i, spot in ipairs(spots) do
		local boat = Instance.new("Folder")
		boat.Name = "Boat" .. i
		boat.Parent = folder
		local hull = PartKit.Box(boat, Vector3.new(12, 2, 5), spot, WOOD_DARK, Enum.Material.Wood)
		hull.Name = "Hull"
		PartKit.Cylinder(boat, 10, 0.5, spot + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0), WOOD, Enum.Material.Wood).Name = "Mast"
		local sail = PartKit.Box(boat, Vector3.new(0.4, 7, 6), spot + Vector3.new(0, 7, 0), Color3.fromRGB(250, 245, 230), Enum.Material.Fabric)
		sail.Name = "Sail"
	end
end

local function buildPalms(folder)
	local spots = {
		Vector3.new(-70, 0, -45),
		Vector3.new(70, 0, -45),
		Vector3.new(-70, 0, 45),
		Vector3.new(70, 0, 45),
		Vector3.new(-110, 0, 0),
		Vector3.new(110, 0, 0),
	}
	for i, spot in ipairs(spots) do
		local palm = Instance.new("Folder")
		palm.Name = "Palm" .. i
		palm.Parent = folder
		local trunk = PartKit.Cylinder(palm, 12, 1.2, spot + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0), TRUNK, Enum.Material.Wood)
		trunk.Name = "Trunk"
		for leaf = 1, 4 do
			local angle = (leaf - 1) * math.pi / 2
			local leafPart = PartKit.Box(palm, Vector3.new(7, 0.3, 1.6), spot + Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * 3.5, 12, math.sin(angle) * 3.5), LEAF, Enum.Material.Grass)
			leafPart.Name = "Leaf" .. leaf
			leafPart.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, math.deg(angle), 25)
		end
	end
end

function World.Build()
	local folder = Instance.new("Folder")
	folder.Name = "BazaarWorld"
	folder.Parent = workspace
	buildWater(folder)
	buildDock(folder)
	local stallAnchors = {}
	for i, position in ipairs(Config.StallPositions) do
		stallAnchors[i] = buildStall(folder, position, i)
	end
	local bases = {}
	for i, position in ipairs(Config.BasePositions) do
		bases[i] = buildBase(folder, position, i)
	end
	buildConveyor(folder)
	buildLighthouse(folder)
	buildLanterns(folder)
	buildBoats(folder)
	buildPalms(folder)
	return {
		Folder = folder,
		Bases = bases,
		StallAnchors = stallAnchors,
		LighthousePosition = Config.LighthousePosition,
	}
end

return World

--!strict

-- Formats documentation prose: Moonwave doc comments (`--[=[ ... ]=]`) in src,
-- and the Markdown files in the repository root
-- Usage (from repo root): lute run .lute/docs.luau [--check]
-- With --check, nothing is written, and the script fails if any file would
-- change (CI runs it this way)
-- by @vuppyan

-- Paragraphs fill each line up to MAX_WIDTH columns, instead of starting each
-- sentence on a new line, and wrapped list items line up with the item's text.
-- Code blocks, tables, headings, Moonwave `@` tags, and lines ending in a hard
-- break are left as they are, and blockquotes are formatted inside the quote.
-- A wrapped line never starts with a token that Markdown or Moonwave would
-- read differently there, such as `*`, `1.`, `#`, `>`, `|`, or `@param`

local fs = require("@std/fs")
local process = require("@std/process")

local MAX_WIDTH = 80
local SRC_DIR = "src"
local MARKDOWN_FILES = { "README.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "CHANGELOG.md" }

-- process.args[1] is this script's path
local argument: string? = process.args[2]
if argument ~= nil and argument ~= "--check" then
    error(`unknown argument "{argument}"`, 0)
end
local checkOnly = argument == "--check"

-- whether `token` would change meaning at the start of a line
local function isRisky(token: string): boolean
    return token == "*"
        or token == "+"
        or token == "-"
        or token == ">"
        or token == "|"
        or string.match(token, "^%d+[%.%)]$") ~= nil
        or string.match(token, "^#+$") ~= nil
        or string.match(token, "^@") ~= nil
        or string.match(token, "^```") ~= nil
        or string.match(token, "^~~~") ~= nil
        or string.match(token, "^=+$") ~= nil
        or string.match(token, "^%-%-+$") ~= nil
end

-- splits text into words, keeping `code spans` that contain spaces together
local function tokenize(text: string): { string }
    local words: { string } = {}
    local current = ""
    local inCode = false
    for i = 1, #text do
        local char = string.sub(text, i, i)
        if char == "`" then
            inCode = not inCode
            current ..= char
        elseif char == " " and not inCode then
            if current ~= "" then
                table.insert(words, current)
            end
            current = ""
        else
            current ..= char
        end
    end
    if current ~= "" then
        table.insert(words, current)
    end
    return words
end

-- fills `words` into lines of at most `width` columns, starting the first
-- line with `first` and the rest with `rest`
local function fill(
    words: { string },
    first: string,
    rest: string,
    width: number
): { string }
    local lines: { string } = {}
    local current: { string } = {}
    local prefix = first
    local length = #prefix

    for _, word in words do
        if #current > 0 and length + 1 + #word > width then
            -- move the previous word down too, so a risky token never starts
            -- a line
            local carried: string? = nil
            if isRisky(word) and #current > 1 then
                carried = table.remove(current)
            end
            table.insert(lines, prefix .. table.concat(current, " "))
            prefix = rest
            current = if carried then { carried, word } else { word }
            length = #prefix + #table.concat(current, " ")
        else
            length += (if #current > 0 then 1 else 0) + #word
            table.insert(current, word)
        end
    end
    if #current > 0 then
        table.insert(lines, prefix .. table.concat(current, " "))
    end
    return lines
end

-- whether `line` must be kept as it is
local function isVerbatim(line: string): boolean
    local text = string.gsub(line, "^%s+", "")
    return string.match(text, "^[@|#<]") ~= nil
        or string.match(text, "^```") ~= nil
        or string.match(text, "^~~~") ~= nil
        or string.match(text, "^%[[^%]]+%]:%s") ~= nil
        or string.match(text, "^%-%-%-+%s*$") ~= nil
        or string.match(text, "^%*%*%*+%s*$") ~= nil
        or string.match(text, "^___+%s*$") ~= nil
        or string.match(line, "  $") ~= nil
        or string.match(line, "\\$") ~= nil
end

local LIST_ITEM_PATTERNS = {
    "^(%s*)([%*%+%-]%s+)(.*)$",
    "^(%s*)(%d+[%.%)]%s+)(.*)$",
}

-- the indent, marker with its spacing, and text of a list item line
local function matchListItem(line: string): (string?, string?, string?)
    for _, pattern in LIST_ITEM_PATTERNS do
        local indent, marker, text = string.match(line, pattern)
        if indent ~= nil then
            return indent, marker, text
        end
    end
    return nil, nil, nil
end

-- formats `lines`, which have no shared indent, to `width` columns
local function format(lines: { string }, width: number): { string }
    local out: { string } = {}
    local words: { string } = {}
    local first, rest = "", ""
    local fence: string? = nil

    local function flush()
        if #words > 0 then
            for _, line in fill(words, first, rest, width) do
                table.insert(out, line)
            end
            words = {}
        end
    end

    local i = 1
    while i <= #lines do
        local line = lines[i]
        local trimmed = string.gsub(line, "^%s+", "")
        trimmed = string.gsub(trimmed, "%s+$", "")

        if fence ~= nil then
            table.insert(out, line)
            if trimmed == fence then
                fence = nil
            end
            i += 1
        elseif
            string.match(trimmed, "^```") or string.match(trimmed, "^~~~")
        then
            flush()
            fence = string.match(trimmed, "^([`~]+)")
            table.insert(out, line)
            i += 1
        elseif trimmed == "" then
            flush()
            table.insert(out, "")
            i += 1
        elseif string.match(line, "^%s*>") then
            -- blockquote: format its contents, then quote them again
            flush()
            local indent = string.match(line, "^(%s*)") :: string
            local inner: { string } = {}
            while i <= #lines do
                local quoted = lines[i]
                if
                    string.sub(quoted, 1, #indent) ~= indent
                    or string.sub(quoted, #indent + 1, #indent + 1) ~= ">"
                then
                    break
                end
                local content = string.sub(quoted, #indent + 2)
                content = string.gsub(content, "^ ", "")
                table.insert(inner, content)
                i += 1
            end
            for _, quotedLine in format(inner, width - #indent - 2) do
                table.insert(
                    out,
                    if quotedLine == ""
                        then `{indent}>`
                        else `{indent}> {quotedLine}`
                )
            end
        elseif isVerbatim(line) then
            flush()
            table.insert(out, line)
            i += 1
        else
            local indent, marker, text = matchListItem(line)
            if indent ~= nil and marker ~= nil and text ~= nil then
                -- list item: wrapped lines line up with the item's text
                flush()
                first = indent .. marker
                rest = string.rep(" ", #first)
                words = tokenize(text)
            else
                if #words == 0 then
                    -- paragraph: keeps its own indent
                    local own = string.match(line, "^(%s*)") :: string
                    first, rest = own, own
                end
                for _, word in tokenize(trimmed) do
                    table.insert(words, word)
                end
            end
            i += 1
        end
    end
    flush()
    return out
end

-- formats every `--[=[ ... ]=]` block in a Luau file
local function formatLuau(lines: { string }): { string }
    local out: { string } = {}
    local i = 1
    while i <= #lines do
        local line = lines[i]
        table.insert(out, line)
        i += 1
        if string.match(line, "%-%-%[=%[%s*$") then
            local block: { string } = {}
            while i <= #lines and not string.match(lines[i], "^%s*%]=%]") do
                table.insert(block, lines[i])
                i += 1
            end

            -- the block's shared indent
            local shared: number? = nil
            for _, blockLine in block do
                if string.match(blockLine, "%S") then
                    local indent = #(string.match(blockLine, "^( *)") :: string)
                    if shared == nil or indent < shared then
                        shared = indent
                    end
                end
            end
            local indent = string.rep(" ", shared or 0)

            local inner: { string } = {}
            for _, blockLine in block do
                table.insert(
                    inner,
                    if string.match(blockLine, "%S")
                        then string.sub(blockLine, #indent + 1)
                        else ""
                )
            end
            for _, formatted in format(inner, MAX_WIDTH - #indent) do
                table.insert(
                    out,
                    if formatted == "" then "" else indent .. formatted
                )
            end
        end
    end
    return out
end

local function splitLines(contents: string): { string }
    contents = string.gsub(contents, "\r\n", "\n")
    local lines: { string } = {}
    for line in string.gmatch(contents, "([^\n]*)\n") do
        table.insert(lines, line)
    end
    -- a last line with no newline after it
    local last = string.match(contents, "([^\n]+)$")
    if last ~= nil then
        table.insert(lines, last)
    end
    return lines
end

local function luauFiles(directory: string, found: { string })
    for _, entry in fs.listDirectory(directory) do
        local path = `{directory}/{entry.name}`
        if entry.type == "dir" then
            luauFiles(path, found)
        elseif entry.type == "file" and string.match(entry.name, "%.luau$") then
            table.insert(found, path)
        end
    end
end

local files: { string } = table.clone(MARKDOWN_FILES)
luauFiles(SRC_DIR, files)
table.sort(files)

local changed: { string } = {}
for _, path in files do
    local original = fs.readFileToString(path)
    local lines = splitLines(original)
    local formatted = if string.match(path, "%.md$")
        then format(lines, MAX_WIDTH)
        else formatLuau(lines)
    local result = table.concat(formatted, "\n") .. "\n"

    if result ~= string.gsub(original, "\r\n", "\n") then
        table.insert(changed, path)
        if not checkOnly then
            fs.writeStringToFile(path, result)
        end
    end
end

if checkOnly then
    if #changed > 0 then
        print("Docs need formatting (run `lute run .lute/docs.luau`):")
        for _, path in changed do
            print(`  {path}`)
        end
        process.exit(1)
    end
    print("Docs are formatted.")
else
    for _, path in changed do
        print(`Formatted {path}`)
    end
    print(`{#changed} file(s) formatted.`)
end

-- Status: experimental
-- Last verified: 2026-06-17
-- Test coverage: no automated coverage
-- Intended use: example; adapt and test before production.

local AnimationLoader = {}
AnimationLoader.__index = AnimationLoader

type AnimationLoaderState = {
    animator: Animator?,
    cache: { [Animation]: AnimationTrack },
    connections: { RBXScriptConnection },
    destroyed: boolean,
}

export type AnimationLoader = typeof(setmetatable({} :: AnimationLoaderState, AnimationLoader))

function AnimationLoader.new(animator: Animator): AnimationLoader
    assert(animator and animator:IsA("Animator"), "AnimationLoader requires a valid Animator")
    local self = setmetatable(
        {
            animator = animator,
            cache = {},
            connections = {},
            destroyed = false,
        } :: AnimationLoaderState,
        AnimationLoader
    )
    return self
end

function AnimationLoader:LoadTrack(
    animation: Animation,
    priority: Enum.AnimationPriority?,
    fadeTime: number?,
    weight: number?,
    speed: number?
): AnimationTrack
    assert(not self.destroyed, "AnimationLoader has been destroyed")
    local animator = assert(self.animator, "AnimationLoader has no Animator")
    local track = self.cache[animation]
    if not track then
        track = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
        self.cache[animation] = track
    end
    track.Priority = priority or Enum.AnimationPriority.Action
    track:Play(fadeTime or 0.1, weight or 1, speed or 1)
    return track
end

function AnimationLoader:PlayById(
    assetId: string,
    priority: Enum.AnimationPriority?,
    fadeTime: number?,
    weight: number?,
    speed: number?
): AnimationTrack?
    local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
    animation.AnimationId = assetId
    local numericId = assetId:match("%d+")
    animation.Name = if numericId then "Anim_" .. numericId else "Anim"
    local track: AnimationTrack = self:LoadTrack(animation, priority, fadeTime, weight, speed)
    self.connections[#self.connections + 1] = track.Stopped:Connect(function()
        self.cache[animation] = nil
        track:Destroy()
        animation:Destroy()
    end)
    return track
end

function AnimationLoader:StopAll(fadeTime: number?)
    for _, track in pairs(self.cache) do
        if track.IsPlaying then
            track:Stop(fadeTime or 0.1)
        end
    end
end

function AnimationLoader:Destroy()
    if self.destroyed then
        return
    end
    self.destroyed = true
    for _, conn in ipairs(self.connections) do
        conn:Disconnect()
    end
    table.clear(self.connections)
    self:StopAll(0)
    table.clear(self.cache)
    self.animator = nil
end

return AnimationLoader

--!strict
--[[
	Compile-time checks for the component authoring API. `luau-lsp analyze` type-checks this file during lint; it is
	never run. A regression in Flux.Props, Component, Children, split, scope, or cleanup surfaces here as a lint
	error.
]]

local Flux = require("../../src")

type ButtonProps = Flux.Props<"TextButton", {
	label: Flux.Reactive<string>,
	variant: Flux.Reactive<"filled" | "tonal">?,
	onClick: (() -> ())?,
}>

local OWN: { "label" | "variant" | "onClick" } = { "label", "variant", "onClick" }

local Button: Flux.Component<ButtonProps, TextButton> = function(props: ButtonProps): TextButton
	local own, rest = Flux.split(props, OWN)
	return Flux.edit(Flux.new("TextButton")({
		Text = own.label,
		Activated = function()
			local onClick = own.onClick
			if onClick then
				onClick()
			end
		end,
	}))(rest)
end

local children: Flux.Children = {
	Button({
		label = "Save",
		variant = "tonal",
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(120, 40),
		onClick = function() end,
	}),
	Flux.show(true, function()
		return Flux.new("Frame")({})
	end),

-- BrainrotData.luau — the twelve original Indonesian street-food brainrots,
-- their rarities, prices, income rates, mutations and the economy formulas.

local Config = require(script.Parent.Config)

local BrainrotData = {}

BrainrotData.Characters = {
	{ Name = "Bakso Bandit", Rarity = "Common", Price = 50, Rate = 1, Body = Color3.fromRGB(150, 100, 60), Blurb = "A round meatball outlaw with a sack." },
	{ Name = "Kerupuk Knight", Rarity = "Common", Price = 120, Rate = 2, Body = Color3.fromRGB(230, 190, 90), Blurb = "A crisp cracker knight with a shield." },
	{ Name = "Cireng Cyclops", Rarity = "Rare", Price = 350, Rate = 5, Body = Color3.fromRGB(240, 225, 200), Blurb = "A chewy disc with one enormous eye." },
	{ Name = "Sate Sensei", Rarity = "Rare", Price = 800, Rate = 9, Body = Color3.fromRGB(120, 70, 30), Blurb = "A skewer master with headband and tiny katana." },
	{ Name = "Gado-Gado Goblin", Rarity = "Epic", Price = 2000, Rate = 18, Body = Color3.fromRGB(90, 160, 70), Blurb = "A green goblin wearing a peanut bowl hat." },
	{ Name = "Es Cendol Cyber", Rarity = "Epic", Price = 4500, Rate = 32, Body = Color3.fromRGB(120, 200, 180), Blurb = "A drink robot with glowing cendol tubes." },
	{ Name = "Soto Sphinx", Rarity = "Legendary", Price = 9000, Rate = 60, Body = Color3.fromRGB(240, 200, 60), Blurb = "A soup-bowl sphinx with a golden crown." },
	{ Name = "Martabak Monster", Rarity = "Legendary", Price = 18000, Rate = 110, Body = Color3.fromRGB(110, 70, 40), Blurb = "A folded pancake beast with chocolate drips." },
	{ Name = "Nasi Padang Paladin", Rarity = "Mythic", Price = 40000, Rate = 220, Body = Color3.fromRGB(250, 245, 235), Blurb = "A rice-mound knight with a rendang sword." },
	{ Name = "Rendang Rex", Rarity = "Mythic", Price = 90000, Rate = 450, Body = Color3.fromRGB(90, 50, 25), Blurb = "A saucy little tyrant with a tiny crown." },
	{ Name = "Es Teh Sultan", Rarity = "Divine", Price = 250000, Rate = 1200, Body = Color3.fromRGB(200, 130, 50), Blurb = "A sultan seated on a giant iced-tea throne." },
	{ Name = "Klepon King", Rarity = "Divine", Price = 500000, Rate = 2000, Body = Color3.fromRGB(60, 170, 90), Blurb = "A green coconut king with a crown and red cape." },
}

BrainrotData.RarityColors = {
	Common = Color3.fromRGB(190, 195, 203),
	Rare = Color3.fromRGB(70, 160, 255),
	Epic = Color3.fromRGB(180, 80, 255),
	Legendary = Color3.fromRGB(255, 155, 55),
	Mythic = Color3.fromRGB(235, 65, 75),
	Divine = Color3.fromRGB(255, 220, 80),
}

BrainrotData.RarityWeights = {
	Common = 45,
	Rare = 25,
	Epic = 15,
	Legendary = 9,
	Mythic = 5,
	Divine = 1,
}

BrainrotData.Mutations = {
	NORMAL = 1,
	GOLD = 2,
	DIAMOND = 3,
	PEDAS = 5,
}

-- Chances for a market offer to carry a mutation.
BrainrotData.MutationRolls = {
	{ Name = "NORMAL", Weight = 80 },
	{ Name = "GOLD", Weight = 12 },
	{ Name = "DIAMOND", Weight = 6 },
	{ Name = "PEDAS", Weight = 2 },
}

local byName = {}
for _, entry in ipairs(BrainrotData.Characters) do
	byName[entry.Name] = entry
end

function BrainrotData.Find(name)
	return byName[name]
end

function BrainrotData.RebirthCost(rebirths)
	local step = rebirths + 1
	return Config.RebirthBaseCost * step * step
end

function BrainrotData.RebirthMultiplier(rebirths)
	return 1 + rebirths * Config.RebirthIncomeBonus
end

function BrainrotData.IncomePerSecond(entry, mutation, rebirths)
	local factor = BrainrotData.Mutations[mutation] or 1
	return entry.Rate * factor * BrainrotData.RebirthMultiplier(rebirths)
end

local function pickWeighted(rng, tableOfWeights, order)
	local total = 0
	for _, key in ipairs(order) do
		total += tableOfWeights[key]
	end
	local roll = rng:NextNumber(0, total)
	local running = 0
	for _, key in ipairs(order) do
		running += tableOfWeights[key]
		if roll <= running then
			return key
		end
	end
	return order[1]
end

function BrainrotData.RandomCharacter(rng)
	local rarity = pickWeighted(rng, BrainrotData.RarityWeights, Config.RarityOrder)
	local pool = {}
	for _, entry in ipairs(BrainrotData.Characters) do
		if entry.Rarity == rarity then
			table.insert(pool, entry)
		end
	end
	return pool[rng:NextInteger(1, #pool)]
end

function BrainrotData.RandomMutation(rng)
	local total = 0
	for _, roll in ipairs(BrainrotData.MutationRolls) do
		total += roll.Weight
	end
	local pick = rng:NextNumber(0, total)
	local running = 0
	for _, roll in ipairs(BrainrotData.MutationRolls) do
		running += roll.Weight
		if pick <= running then
			return roll.Name
		end
	end
	return "NORMAL"
end

return BrainrotData

--!strict

-- Type checks the typing type function tests in tests/typing
-- Usage (from repo root): lute run .lute/typing.luau [--no-flags-enabled]
-- Pass --no-flags-enabled to check with Studio's Luau flags instead of every
-- flag luau-lsp knows (see .lute/ci.luau)
-- by @vuppyan

-- tests/typing/valid.luau must type check with no errors.
-- Every file in tests/typing/errors must fail to type check with exactly the
-- expected errors: a `-- error: <text>` comment expects an error containing
-- `<text>` on the next line of code, and any other error fails the check.

local fs = require("@std/fs")
local process = require("@std/process")

local VALID_FILE = "tests/typing/valid.luau"
local ERRORS_DIR = "tests/typing/errors"

-- process.args[1] is this script's path
local extraFlag: string? = process.args[2]
if extraFlag ~= nil and extraFlag ~= "--no-flags-enabled" then
    error(`unknown argument "{extraFlag}"`, 0)
end

type Expectation = {
    line: number,
    text: string,
    found: boolean,
}

type Diagnostic = {
    line: number,
    message: string,
}

local function analyze(path: string, stdio: process.StdioKind?)
    -- src is ignored since it is checked separately with ROBLOX globals
    local args = {
        "luau-lsp",
        "analyze",
        "--platform=standard",
        "--flag:LuauSolverV2=true",
        "--ignore=src/**",
    }
    if extraFlag ~= nil then
        table.insert(args, extraFlag)
    end
    table.insert(args, path)
    return process.run(args, { stdio = stdio })
end

-- reads the `-- error: <text>` comments in `source`, each expecting an error
-- on the next line of code
local function readExpectations(source: string): { Expectation }
    local expectations: { Expectation } = {}
    local pending: { string } = {}

    local lineNumber = 0
    for line in string.gmatch(source .. "\n", "([^\n]*)\n") do
        lineNumber += 1
        line = string.gsub(line, "\r$", "")

        local text = string.match(line, "^%s*%-%-%s*error:%s*(.-)%s*$")
        if text then
            table.insert(pending, text)
        elseif string.match(line, "^%s*$") == nil then
            for _, pendingText in pending do
                table.insert(
                    expectations,
                    { line = lineNumber, text = pendingText, found = false }
                )
            end
            table.clear(pending)
        end
    end

    if #pending > 0 then
        error(`"-- error:" comment with no code after it`, 0)
    end
    return expectations
end

-- reads `file(line,col): Kind: message` diagnostics from analyzer output
local function readDiagnostics(output: string): { Diagnostic }
    local diagnostics: { Diagnostic } = {}
    for line in string.gmatch(output, "[^\r\n]+") do
        local lineNumber, message =
            string.match(line, "%((%d+),%d+%): %a+: (.*)$")
        if lineNumber and message then
            table.insert(
                diagnostics,
                { line = tonumber(lineNumber) :: number, message = message }
            )
        end
    end
    return diagnostics
end

-- returns a list of problems with the errors in `path`
local function checkErrorsFile(path: string): { string }
    local expectations = readExpectations(fs.readFileToString(path))
    local result = analyze(path)
    local diagnostics = readDiagnostics(result.stdout .. "\n" .. result.stderr)

    local problems: { string } = {}
    if #expectations == 0 then
        table.insert(problems, `{path}: no "-- error:" comments`)
    end

    for _, diagnostic in diagnostics do
        local expected = false
        for _, expectation in expectations do
            if
                expectation.line == diagnostic.line
                and string.find(diagnostic.message, expectation.text, 1, true)
            then
                expectation.found = true
                expected = true
            end
        end
        if not expected then
            table.insert(
                problems,
                `{path}:{diagnostic.line}: unexpected error: {diagnostic.message}`
            )
        end
    end

    for _, expectation in expectations do
        if not expectation.found then
            table.insert(
                problems,
                `{path}:{expectation.line}: missing error: {expectation.text}`
            )
        end
    end

    return problems
end

local failed = false

print(`--- {VALID_FILE}`)
if not analyze(VALID_FILE, "inherit").ok then
    print(`{VALID_FILE} failed to type check`)
    failed = true
end

local errorFiles: { string } = {}
for _, entry in fs.listDirectory(ERRORS_DIR) do
    if entry.type == "file" and string.match(entry.name, "%.luau$") then
        table.insert(errorFiles, `{ERRORS_DIR}/{entry.name}`)
    end
end
table.sort(errorFiles)

for _, path in errorFiles do
    print(`--- {path}`)
    local problems = checkErrorsFile(path)
    for _, problem in problems do
        print(problem)
    end
    if #problems > 0 then
        failed = true
    end
end

if failed then
    process.exit(1)
end
print("All typing checks passed.")

    endEffector: BasePart | Bone,
    chainRoot: BasePart | Bone,
    target: Attachment | BasePart,
    type: Enum.IKControlType?,
    smoothTime: number?,
    p: number?,
}

function IKSetup.create(config: IKChainConfig): IKControl
    local ik = Instance.new("IKControl")
    ik.Type = config.type or Enum.IKControlType.Position
    ik.EndEffector = config.endEffector
    ik.ChainRoot = config.chainRoot
    if config.target:IsA("Attachment") then
        ik.Target = config.target :: Attachment
    else
        local targetAttachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
        targetAttachment.Name = "IKTarget"
        targetAttachment.Parent = config.target :: BasePart
        ik.Target = targetAttachment
    end
    ik.SmoothTime = config.smoothTime or 0.1
    ik.Weight = config.p or 1
    ik.Parent = config.parent
    ik.Enabled = true
    return ik
end

function IKSetup.createHingeConstraint(
    parent: BasePart,
    attachment0: Attachment,
    attachment1: Attachment,
    lowerAngle: number?,
    upperAngle: number?
): HingeConstraint
    local hinge = Instance.new("HingeConstraint")
    hinge.Attachment0 = attachment0
    hinge.Attachment1 = attachment1
    hinge.LimitsEnabled = true
    hinge.LowerAngle = lowerAngle or -90
    hinge.UpperAngle = upperAngle or 90
    hinge.Restitution = 0
    hinge.Parent = parent
    return hinge
end

return IKSetup

	node takes the property's type, `#Tag` / `_tag_Tag` gives `boolean`, `$Attr` / `_attr_Attr` or an unknown key gives
	`any`, and `_Prop` / `__EVENT` listeners receive the property's value. Lint type-checks this file; it is never run.

local Flux = require("../../src")

local box = Instance.new("TextBox")

local text: Flux.Node<string> = Flux.property(box, "Text")

Flux.edit(box)({

	_AbsoluteSize = function(_value: Vector2) end,

		AbsoluteSize = function(_value: Vector2) end, -- read-only properties have listeners too

})

--!strict

-- Checks that every file holding the library version agrees
-- Usage (from repo root): lute run .lute/version.luau [expected version]
-- With an expected version (for example 1.2.3), also checks that the files
-- hold that version and that no `@since [UNRELEASED]` or
-- `@deprecated [UNRELEASED]` tags are left in src, which is run before tagging a
-- release
-- by @vuppyan

local fs = require("@std/fs")
local process = require("@std/process")

-- { file, pattern capturing the version }
local SOURCES: { { string } } = {
    { "src/luautils/init.luau", 'Luautils%.VERSION%s*=%s*"([^"]+)"' },
    { "wally.toml", '\nversion%s*=%s*"([^"]+)"' },
    { "pesde.toml", '\nversion%s*=%s*"([^"]+)"' },
    -- first numbered heading is the latest release; UNRELEASED never matches
    { "CHANGELOG.md", "\n## %[v?(%d+%.%d+%.%d+[^%]]*)%]" },
}

-- docs tags for API added or deprecated since the last release, replaced with
-- the version when releasing
local UNRELEASED_TAGS = { "@since", "@deprecated" }
local SRC_DIR = "src"

local found: { { string } } = {}
for _, source in SOURCES do
    local path, pattern = source[1], source[2]
    local version = string.match(fs.readFileToString(path), pattern)
    if version == nil then
        print(`Could not find a version in {path}`)
        process.exit(1)
    end
    table.insert(found, { path, version })
end

-- process.args[1] is this script's path
local argument: string? = process.args[2]
if argument ~= nil then
    -- accept both 1.2.3 and v1.2.3
    argument = string.gsub(argument, "^v", "")
end
local expected = argument or found[1][2]
local ok = true
for _, entry in found do
    print(`Found {entry[1]}: {entry[2]}`)
    if entry[2] ~= expected then
        ok = false
    end
end

if not ok then
    if argument ~= nil then
        print(`Version mismatch: expected {expected} in every file`)
    else
        print("Version mismatch: bump every file together")
    end
    process.exit(1)
end

local function luauFiles(directory: string, files: { string })
    for _, entry in fs.listDirectory(directory) do
        local path = `{directory}/{entry.name}`
        if entry.type == "dir" then
            luauFiles(path, files)
        elseif entry.type == "file" and string.match(entry.name, "%.luau$") then
            table.insert(files, path)
        end
    end
end

-- only checked for a release, since feature branches add these tags
if argument ~= nil then
    local files: { string } = {}
    luauFiles(SRC_DIR, files)
    table.sort(files)

    local leftover = 0
    for _, path in files do
        local lines = string.split(fs.readFileToString(path), "\n")
        for lineNumber, line in lines do
            for _, tag in UNRELEASED_TAGS do
                if string.find(line, `{tag} [UNRELEASED]`, 1, true) then
                    print(`{path}:{lineNumber}: {tag} [UNRELEASED]`)
                    leftover += 1
                end
            end
        end
    end

    if leftover > 0 then
        print(
            `Found {leftover} [UNRELEASED] tags: replace them with v{expected}`
        )
        process.exit(1)
    end
end

--!strict
-- Status: experimental
-- Last verified: 2026-06-17
-- Test coverage: no automated coverage
-- Intended use: example; adapt and test before production.

local TweenHelper = {}

export type TweenConfig = {
    duration: number,
    easingStyle: Enum.EasingStyle?,
    easingDirection: Enum.EasingDirection?,
    repeatCount: number?,
    reverses: boolean?,
    delayTime: number?,
}

local TweenService: TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local function buildTweenInfo(config: TweenConfig): TweenInfo
    return TweenInfo.new(
        config.duration,
        config.easingStyle or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad,
        config.easingDirection or Enum.EasingDirection.Out,
        config.repeatCount or 0,
        config.reverses or false,
        config.delayTime or 0
    )
end

function TweenHelper.tween(
    instance: Instance,
    properties: { [string]: any },
    config: TweenConfig
): Tween
    local info = buildTweenInfo(config)
    local tween = TweenService:Create(instance, info, properties)
    tween:Play()
    return tween
end

function TweenHelper.tweenAsync(
    instance: Instance,
    properties: { [string]: any },
    config: TweenConfig
): boolean
    local tween = TweenHelper.tween(instance, properties, config)
    local completed = false
    local conn: RBXScriptConnection?
    conn = tween.Completed:Connect(function()
        completed = true
        if conn then
            conn:Disconnect()
        end
    end)
    while not completed do
        task.wait()
    end
    return completed
end

function TweenHelper.sequence(steps: {
    {
        instance: Instance,
        properties: { [string]: any },
        config: TweenConfig,
    }
}): ()
    local current = 1
    local function playNext()
        if current > #steps then
            return
        end
        local step = steps[current]
        current += 1
        local tween = TweenHelper.tween(step.instance, step.properties, step.config)
        local conn: RBXScriptConnection?
        conn = tween.Completed:Once(function()
            if conn then
                conn:Disconnect()
            end
            playNext()
        end)
    end
    playNext()
end

return TweenHelper

	return (acc or 0) + cur - (prev or 0)
end))

	Flux.computed(Flux.on({ count, name }, function(cur: { number | string }, _prev: { number | string }?)
		return cur[1]
	end))
local _onEffect = Flux.effect(Flux.on(count, function(cur: number): ()
	local _ = cur + 1
end))

local tweenObj: Flux.Tween<number> = Flux.tween(count, TweenInfo.new(0.2))
local _setTween: number = tweenObj:set(10)
local _setSpring: number = spring:set(10)
local _snappedTween: Flux.Tween<number> = tweenObj:snap():snap(5)
local _snappedSpring: Flux.Spring<number> = spring:snap():snap(10)

local _flexNum: UIFlexItem = Flux.flex(1)
local _flexCustom: UIFlexItem = Flux.flex("custom")
local _flexCfg: UIFlexItem = Flux.flex({ mode = "custom", grow = 2, shrink = 1, lineAlign = "center" })
local _flexSig: UIFlexItem = Flux.flex(count)
local _scaleDefault: UIScale = Flux.scale()
local _scaleSig: UIScale = Flux.scale(count)

local _mappedFallback: Node<{ string | number }> = Flux.forValue(function()
	return { "a", "b" }
end, function(_index, value)
	return string.upper(value)
end, function()
	return 0
end)
local _indexedFallback: Node<{ number | string }> = Flux.forIndex(
	Flux.signal({ 1, 2 }),
	function(_index, item: Node<number>)

	end,
	function()
		return "empty"
	end
)
local _keyedFallback: Node<{ string | boolean }> = Flux.forKey(
	Flux.signal({ { id = 1, label = "A" } } :: { KeyedRow }),
	function(row)
		return row.id
	end,
	function(index, row: Node<KeyedRow>)
		return `{index()}:{row().label}`
	end,
	function()
		return false
	end
)

	updatedNode,
	_updatedSpring,
	activatedNode,
	downNode,
	customMaybe,
	customSeeded,
	retriedSafe,
	staticSafe,
	prevMemo,
	prevFast,
	onSingle,
	onTuple,
	_onEffect,
	_setTween,
	_setSpring,
	_snappedTween,
	_snappedSpring,
	_flexNum,
	_flexCustom,
	_flexCfg,
	_flexSig,
	_scaleDefault,
	_scaleSig,
	_mappedFallback,
	_indexedFallback,
	_keyedFallback,
}

local PartKit = {}

function PartKit.Part(parent, props)
	local part = Instance.new("Part")
	part.Anchored = true
	part.CanCollide = true
	for key, value in pairs(props) do
		part[key] = value
	end
	part.Parent = parent
	return part
end

function PartKit.Ball(parent, radius, position, color, material)
	return PartKit.Part(parent, {
		Name = "Ball",
		Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball,
		Size = Vector3.new(radius * 2, radius * 2, radius * 2),
		Position = position,
		Color = color,
		Material = material or Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic,
	})
end

function PartKit.Box(parent, size, position, color, material)
	return PartKit.Part(parent, {
		Name = "Box",
		Shape = Enum.PartType.Block,
		Size = size,
		Position = position,
		Color = color,
		Material = material or Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic,
	})
end

function PartKit.Cylinder(parent, length, diameter, position, color, material)
	return PartKit.Part(parent, {
		Name = "Cylinder",
		Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder,
		Size = Vector3.new(length, diameter, diameter),
		Position = position,
		Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 0, 90),
		Color = color,
		Material = material or Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic,
	})
end

function PartKit.Wedge(parent, size, position, color, material)
	return PartKit.Part(parent, {
		Name = "Wedge",
		Shape = Enum.PartType.Wedge,
		Size = size,
		Position = position,
		Color = color,
		Material = material or Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic,
	})
end

-- A floating name plate above a model. parent must be a BasePart.
function PartKit.Label(parent, text, textColor, size)
	local gui = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	gui.Name = "FloatLabel"
	gui.Size = UDim2.new(0, 160, 0, 44)
	gui.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, size, 0)
	gui.AlwaysOnTop = true
	gui.Parent = parent
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Text"
	label.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
	label.TextSize = 15
	label.TextColor3 = textColor
	label.TextStrokeTransparency = 0.2
	label.Text = text
	label.Parent = gui
	return gui
end

-- Two round eyes and a smile on the front (+Z face) of a ball body.
function PartKit.Face(body, radius, eyeColor)
	local front = body.Position + Vector3.new(0, radius * 0.25, radius * 0.85)
	local eyeSize = radius * 0.28
	PartKit.Ball(body.Parent, eyeSize, front + Vector3.new(-radius * 0.38, 0, 0), eyeColor or Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 25))
	PartKit.Ball(body.Parent, eyeSize, front + Vector3.new(radius * 0.38, 0, 0), eyeColor or Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 25))
	local mouth = PartKit.Box(
		body.Parent,
		Vector3.new(radius * 0.7, radius * 0.16, radius * 0.1),
		body.Position + Vector3.new(0, -radius * 0.3, radius * 0.9),
		Color3.fromRGB(30, 15, 15)
	)
	mouth.Name = "Mouth"
end

return PartKit

--!strict
--[[
	Compile-time checks for `Flux.Sync`: shared signals, validators, per-player `:of` / `:clear`, `:unreliable`,
	`Flux.Sync.ready`, and `Flux.Unwrap`. Lint type-checks this file; it is never run.
]]

local Flux = require("../../src")

type Node<T> = Flux.Node<T>
type Reactive<T> = Flux.Reactive<T>

local coins = Flux.Sync("Coins", 0)
local name = Flux.Sync("Name", "Kohl")
local theme = Flux.Sync("Theme", "Dark", function(_player: Player, value: string)
	return value == "Dark" or value == "Light"
end)
local dynamic = Flux.Sync.Dynamic
local volume: Flux.SyncSignal<number> = Flux.Sync("Volume", 5, function(_, value)
	return true, math.clamp(value, 0, 10)
end)

local n: number = coins()
local s: string = name:get()
local t: string = theme:peek()
coins:set(5)
name:set("Kohl2")
dynamic("anything")
assert(coins() == 5 and name() == "Kohl2", "synced")

local function forPlayer(player: Player)
	local own: Flux.State<number> = coins:of(player)
	own:set(10)
	coins:clear(player)
end

local chained: Flux.SyncSignal<number> = coins:unreliable(true):validate(function(_, value)
	if type(value) ~= "number" or value ~= value then
		return false
	end
	return true, math.clamp(value, 0, 100)
end)

local asNode: Node<number> = coins
local label: Reactive<string> = name
local unwrapped: Flux.Unwrap<Flux.SyncSignal<number>> = 1
local doubled = Flux.computed(function()
	return coins() * 2
end)
Flux.Sync.flush()
local ready: boolean = Flux.Sync.ready()
assert(coins:peek() == 5)
local updatedCoins: Flux.SyncSignal<number> = coins:update(function(cur: number): number
	return cur + 1
end)

return { ready, n, s, t, forPlayer, chained, asNode, label, unwrapped, doubled, volume, updatedCoins }

-- Status: experimental
-- Last verified: 2026-06-17
-- Test coverage: no automated coverage
-- Intended use: example; adapt and test before production.

--[[
    AudioBus.lua
    A small music/SFX bus helper using the modern audio graph.

    - Creates separate AudioFader instances for Music and SFX buses.
    - Wires AudioPlayers (you provide) through the appropriate bus to a shared
      AudioDeviceOutput.
    - Supports ducking: temporarily lower music volume while SFX play, then
      restore.

    Usage:
        local AudioBus = require(path.to.AudioBus)
        local bus = AudioBus.new()

        local musicPlayer = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
        musicPlayer.AssetId = "rbxassetid://MUSIC_ID"
        musicPlayer.Looping = true
        bus:attachMusic(musicPlayer)
        musicPlayer:Play()

        local sfxPlayer = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
        sfxPlayer.AssetId = "rbxassetid://SFX_ID"
        bus:attachSfx(sfxPlayer)
        bus:playSfxWithDuck(sfxPlayer, 0.3, 1.5) -- duck music to 0.3 for 1.5s
]]

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService")

local AudioBus = {}
AudioBus.__index = AudioBus

export type AudioBus = typeof(setmetatable(
    {} :: {
        musicFader: AudioFader,
        sfxFader: AudioFader,
        output: AudioDeviceOutput,
        musicVolume: number,
    },
    AudioBus
))

local function makeFader(parent: Instance, name: string, volume: number): AudioFader
    local fader = Instance.new("AudioFader")
    fader.Name = name
    fader.Volume = volume
    fader.Parent = parent
    return fader
end

local function wire(source: Instance, target: Instance, parent: Instance): Wire
    local w = Instance.new("Wire")
    w.SourceInstance = source
    w.TargetInstance = target
    w.Parent = parent
    return w
end

function AudioBus.new(): AudioBus
    local output = Instance.new("AudioDeviceOutput")
    output.Name = "BusOutput"
    output.Parent = SoundService

    local musicFader = makeFader(SoundService, "MusicFader", 1)
    local sfxFader = makeFader(SoundService, "SfxFader", 1)

    -- Bus → output
    wire(musicFader, output, SoundService)
    wire(sfxFader, output, SoundService)

    return setmetatable({
        output = output,
        musicFader = musicFader,
        sfxFader = sfxFader,
        musicVolume = 1,
    }, AudioBus) :: AudioBus
end

function AudioBus:attachMusic(player: AudioPlayer): ()
    -- Ensure the player has a parent so it can be wired
    if not player.Parent then
        player.Parent = SoundService
    end
    wire(player, self.musicFader, SoundService)
end

function AudioBus:attachSfx(player: AudioPlayer): ()
    if not player.Parent then
        player.Parent = SoundService
    end
    wire(player, self.sfxFader, SoundService)
end

function AudioBus:setMusicVolume(volume: number, fadeTime: number?): ()
    fadeTime = fadeTime or 0.2
    self.musicVolume = volume
    local tween = TweenService:Create(self.musicFader, TweenInfo.new(fadeTime), { Volume = volume })
    tween:Play()
end

function AudioBus:playSfxWithDuck(player: AudioPlayer, duckTo: number?, duckDuration: number?): ()
    duckTo = duckTo or 0.3
    duckDuration = duckDuration or 1.5
    local original = self.musicVolume
    self:setMusicVolume(duckTo, 0.1)
    player:Play()
    task.delay(duckDuration, function()
        self:setMusicVolume(original, 0.5)
    end)
end

function AudioBus:destroy(): ()
    for _, obj in ipairs({ self.musicFader, self.sfxFader, self.output }) do
        if obj and obj.Parent then
            obj:Destroy()
        end
    end
end

return AudioBus

--!strict

-- retry function
-- by @vuppyan

local Core = require("../Core")
type Result<T, E> = Core.Result<T, E>

local typing = require("../Core/typing")
type Supplier<T> = typing.Supplier<T>

local fail = Core.Errors.errorWithScope("Async")

--[=[
    Options for `retry`.

    @interface RetryOptions
    @within Async
    @since v0.1.0
    @field attempts number -- The total number of attempts, including the first
    @field delay number? -- The seconds to wait between attempts (defaults to not waiting)
    @field sleep ((seconds: number) -> ())? -- The function used to wait between attempts (defaults to `task.wait`, which only exists in ROBLOX, so pass one when using `delay` elsewhere)
]=]
export type RetryOptions = {
    read attempts: number,
    read delay: number?,
    read sleep: ((seconds: number) -> ())?,
}

--[=[
    Calls `attempt` until it returns "ok" or `options.attempts` is reached,
    returning the first "ok" or the last "err".

    Wrap functions that throw with `Result.try` (one return value) or
    `Result.tryPack` (all return values).

    There is no wait after the last attempt.

    ```lua
    -- a throwing function with one return value
    local data = retry(function()
        return Result.try(store.GetAsync, store, key)
    end, { attempts = 3, delay = 1 })
    -- multiple return values
    local res = retry(function()
        return Result.tryPack(getPair, a, b)
    end, { attempts = 3 })
    local packed = res:unwrap()
    local x, y = table.unpack(packed, 1, packed.n)
    -- a function that already returns a Result
    local parsed = retry(function()
        return Duration.tryParse(readSetting())
    end, { attempts = 5 })
    ```

    @function retry
    @within Async
    @since v0.1.0
    @param attempt Supplier<Result<T, E>> -- The function to call
    @param options RetryOptions -- The retry options
    @return Result<T, E> -- The result of `attempt`
    @error "[Async.retry()]: Attempts must be a positive integer" -- Thrown if `options.attempts` is not a positive integer
]=]
return function<T, E>(
    attempt: Supplier<Result<T, E>>,
    options: RetryOptions
): Result<T, E>
    local attempts = options.attempts
    if attempts < 1 or attempts % 1 ~= 0 then
        fail("Attempts must be a positive integer", nil, "retry")
    end

    local result = attempt()
    for _ = 2, attempts do
        if result:isOk() then
            break
        end
        if options.delay then
            (options.sleep or task.wait)(options.delay)
        end
        result = attempt()
    end
    return result
end

--[[
ServiceHelper.lua

local ServiceHelper = require(...)
local Players = ServiceHelper.getService("Players")

]]

local ServiceHelper = {}

function ServiceHelper.getService(serviceName: string): Instance
    return game:GetService(serviceName)
end

local DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: number = 10

function ServiceHelper.requireModule<T>(moduleName: string, parent: Instance?, timeout: number?): T
    local moduleParent = parent or game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
    local module = moduleParent:WaitForChild(moduleName, timeout or DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
    if module and module:IsA("ModuleScript") then
        return require(module) :: T
    end
    error("Module not found or not a ModuleScript: " .. moduleName)
end

return ServiceHelper

--[[
BudgetMonitor.lua
Utilities for inspecting and configuring DataStore request budgets at server startup.
Call early in a Script under ServerScriptService (once per server).

Example:
local BudgetMonitor = require(...)
BudgetMonitor.configureForBusyServer()
BudgetMonitor.printAllBudgets()
]]

local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local BudgetMonitor = {}

type RequestTypeEntry = {
    name: string,
    requestType: Enum.DataStoreRequestType,
}

local REQUEST_TYPES: { RequestTypeEntry } = {
    { name = "StandardRead", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardRead },
    { name = "StandardWrite", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardWrite },
    { name = "StandardList", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardList },
    { name = "StandardRemove", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardRemove },
    { name = "OrderedRead", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedRead },
    { name = "OrderedWrite", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedWrite },
    { name = "OrderedRemove", requestType = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedRemove },
    -- Note: GetVersionAsync/GetVersionAtTimeAsync count as StandardRead, not separate budget categories.
    -- OrderedList is intentionally omitted: GetRequestBudgetForRequestType always returns 0 for it.
}

local REQUEST_TYPES_BY_NAME: { [string]: Enum.DataStoreRequestType } = {
    StandardRead = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardRead,
    StandardWrite = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardWrite,
    StandardList = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardList,
    StandardRemove = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardRemove,
    OrderedRead = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedRead,
    OrderedWrite = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedWrite,
    OrderedList = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedList,
    OrderedRemove = Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedRemove,
}

function BudgetMonitor.printAllBudgets()
    print("=== Current DataStore Request Budgets ===")
    for _, entry in REQUEST_TYPES do
        local budget = DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType(entry.requestType)
        print(string.format("%-20s : %d", entry.name, budget))
    end
    print("OrderedList            : budget inspection always returns 0")
end

function BudgetMonitor.configureForBusyServer()
    -- Example aggressive but reasonable settings for a popular game or migration server.
    -- Tune based on your actual concurrent player count and workload.
    -- Call this ONLY during server initialization, once per type.

    local function safeSet(
        requestTypeName: string,
        requestType: Enum.DataStoreRequestType,
        base: number,
        perPlayer: number
    )
        local ok, err = pcall(function()
            DataStoreService:SetRateLimitForRequestType(requestType, base, perPlayer)
        end)
        if ok then
            print("Configured", requestTypeName, "base=", base, "perPlayer=", perPlayer)
        else
            warn("Failed to set rate limit for", requestTypeName, err)
        end
    end

    -- These are examples — respect the per-type constraints documented in the class reference.
    -- The per-player StandardWrite value here matches the Roblox default (40). Lowering it reduces
    -- per-server burst but can cause write throttling under load; raising it increases headroom
    -- but also raises the ceiling on how much a single server can consume.
    safeSet("StandardRead", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardRead, 2000, 50)
    safeSet("StandardWrite", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardWrite, 1500, 40)
    safeSet("StandardList", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardList, 300, 5)
    safeSet("StandardRemove", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.StandardRemove, 1000, 20)

    safeSet("OrderedRead", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedRead, 1500, 40)
    safeSet("OrderedWrite", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedWrite, 1000, 20)
    -- OrderedList: SetRateLimitForRequestType accepts the enum, but GetRequestBudgetForRequestType
    -- always returns 0 for it, so the limit cannot be inspected at runtime.
    safeSet("OrderedList", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedList, 150, 3)
    safeSet("OrderedRemove", Enum.DataStoreRequestType.OrderedRemove, 800, 15)
end

function BudgetMonitor.waitForAnyBudget(requestTypeName: string, timeout: number?): boolean
    local enumItem = REQUEST_TYPES_BY_NAME[requestTypeName]
    if not enumItem then
        return false
    end
    if requestTypeName == "OrderedList" then
        warn(
            "Cannot wait for budget of "
                .. requestTypeName
                .. "; GetRequestBudgetForRequestType always returns 0 for this type."
        )
        return false
    end

    local start = os.clock()
    while DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType(enumItem) <= 0 do
        if os.clock() - start > (timeout or 30) then
            return false
        end
        task.wait(0.25)
    end
    return true
end

return BudgetMonitor
