-- MoneyService: every dollar in the game. It owns the leaderstats (Cash,
-- Income, Rebirths), pays out one second of stand income every second,
-- charges for purchases and stand upgrades, pays for sales, runs rebirth,
-- and keeps the top-three leaderboard fresh. Rebirth counts persist in the
-- BlitzRebirthsV1 DataStore, so a returning player keeps their prestige.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local BrainrotData = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Shared.BrainrotData)

local MoneyService = {}

local rebirthStore = nil
local rebirths = {}

local function getStore()
	if rebirthStore ~= nil then
		return rebirthStore
	end
	local ok, store = pcall(function()
		return DataStoreService:GetDataStore(BrainrotData.DataStoreName)
	end)
	if ok then
		rebirthStore = store
	end
	return rebirthStore
end

function MoneyService.init(ctx)
	local world = ctx.world
	local events = ctx.events
	local remotes = ctx.remotes
	local baseService = ctx.services.BaseService

	local function setupPlayer(player)
		local leaderstats = Instance.new("Folder")
		leaderstats.Name = "leaderstats"
		leaderstats.Parent = player
		local cash = Instance.new("IntValue")
		cash.Name = "Cash"
		cash.Value = BrainrotData.Economy.startCash
		cash.Parent = leaderstats
		local income = Instance.new("IntValue")
		income.Name = "Income"
		income.Value = 0
		income.Parent = leaderstats
		local rebirthCount = Instance.new("IntValue")
		rebirthCount.Name = "Rebirths"
		rebirthCount.Value = 0
		rebirthCount.Parent = leaderstats
		rebirths[player] = 0
		local store = getStore()
		if store then
			local ok, saved = pcall(function()
				return store:GetAsync(tostring(player.UserId))
			end)
			if ok and typeof(saved) == "number" then
				rebirths[player] = saved
				rebirthCount.Value = saved
			end
		end
	end

	local function savePlayer(player)
		local store = getStore()
		if store and rebirths[player] ~= nil then
			pcall(function()
				store:SetAsync(tostring(player.UserId), rebirths[player])
			end)
		end
	end

	local function cashValue(player)
		local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
		if not stats then
			return 0
		end
		local cash = stats:FindFirstChild("Cash")
		return cash and cash.Value or 0
	end

	local function setCash(player, amount)
		local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
		if not stats then
			return
		end
		local cash = stats:FindFirstChild("Cash")
		if cash then
			cash.Value = math.max(0, math.floor(amount))
		end
	end

	local function incomePerSecond(player)
		local total = 0
		local count = baseService.getStandCount(player)
		for slot = 1, count do
			local record = baseService.getSlot(player, slot)
			if record and record.entry then
				total += BrainrotData.characterIncome(record.entry, record.mutationId)
			end
		end
		return total * BrainrotData.incomeMultiplier(rebirths[player] or 0)
	end

	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(setupPlayer)
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		savePlayer(player)
		rebirths[player] = nil
	end)
	for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
		setupPlayer(player)
	end

	-- Income loop: every second, every placed character earns its income.
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(1)
			for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
				local perSecond = incomePerSecond(player)
				local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
				if stats then
					local incomeValue = stats:FindFirstChild("Income")
					if incomeValue then
						incomeValue.Value = math.floor(perSecond)
					end
				end
				if perSecond > 0 then
					setCash(player, cashValue(player) + perSecond)
				end
			end
		end
	end)

	-- A conveyor purchase: charge the cash, then let BaseService place it.
	events.PurchaseRequested.Event:Connect(function(player, entry, mutationId, price, model, isGolden)
		if cashValue(player) >= price then
			setCash(player, cashValue(player) - price)
			events.PurchaseApproved:Fire(player, entry, mutationId, price, model, isGolden)
		else
			events.PurchaseDenied:Fire(player, "Not enough cash", model)
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Not enough cash for " .. entry.name .. "!")
		end
	end)

	-- Refunds (for example when a purchase was approved but no stand was free).
	events.Refund.Event:Connect(function(player, amount)
		setCash(player, cashValue(player) + amount)
	end)

	-- Generic charges (stand upgrades): deduct on approval, deny otherwise.
	events.ChargeRequested.Event:Connect(function(player, amount, purpose, payload)
		if cashValue(player) >= amount then
			setCash(player, cashValue(player) - amount)
			events.ChargeApproved:Fire(player, purpose, payload)
		else
			events.ChargeDenied:Fire(player, purpose, { reason = "Not enough cash" })
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Not enough cash!")
		end
	end)

	-- Selling a character from one of your own stands: half the buy price.
	events.SellRequested.Event:Connect(function(player, slot)
		local record = baseService.getSlot(player, slot)
		if not record or not record.entry then
			return
		end
		local payout = math.floor(record.entry.price * BrainrotData.Economy.sellFraction)
		setCash(player, cashValue(player) + payout)
		if record.model then
			record.model:Destroy()
		end
		events.CharacterRemoved:Fire(player, slot)
		remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Sold " .. record.entry.name .. " for $" .. tostring(payout) .. ".")
	end)

	-- Rebirth: pay the price, gain a permanent +50% income (plus milestone
	-- bonuses), and start the cash pile over.
	remotes.Rebirth.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
		local count = rebirths[player] or 0
		local cost = BrainrotData.rebirthCost(count)
		if cashValue(player) < cost then
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Rebirth costs $" .. tostring(cost) .. ".")
			return
		end
		setCash(player, BrainrotData.Economy.startCash)
		rebirths[player] = count + 1
		local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
		if stats then
			local rebirthValue = stats:FindFirstChild("Rebirths")
			if rebirthValue then
				rebirthValue.Value = count + 1
			end
		end
		savePlayer(player)
		local milestone = BrainrotData.milestoneBonus(count + 1)
		local message = "Rebirth " .. tostring(count + 1) .. "! Income +" .. tostring(math.floor(BrainrotData.incomeMultiplier(count + 1) * 100 - 100)) .. "%."
		if milestone > 0 then
			message ..= " Milestone bonus active!"
		end
		remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, message)
	end)

	-- Leaderboard: the three richest players, refreshed every ten seconds
	-- on the board in the middle of the island and on every client.
	local function refreshLeaderboard()
		local ranked = {}
		for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
			table.insert(ranked, { name = player.Name, cash = cashValue(player) })
		end
		table.sort(ranked, function(a, b)
			return a.cash > b.cash
		end)
		local top = {}
		for i = 1, 3 do
			if ranked[i] then
				top[i] = ranked[i]
			else
				top[i] = { name = "---", cash = 0 }
			end
		end
		local gui = world.boardGui
		for i = 1, 3 do
			local line = gui:FindFirstChild("BoardLine" .. tostring(i))
			if line then
				line.Text = tostring(i) .. ". " .. top[i].name .. " - $" .. tostring(top[i].cash)
			end
		end
		remotes.TopThree:FireAllClients(top)
	end

	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(10)
			refreshLeaderboard()
		end
	end)
	refreshLeaderboard()
end

return MoneyService

--!strict
-- Global "most wins" board in the lobby, backed by an OrderedDataStore.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local Config = require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Config)

local LeaderboardBuffer = require(script.Parent.Parent.Data.LeaderboardBuffer)
local RobloxStore = require(script.Parent.Parent.Data.RobloxStore)
local ArenaService = require(script.Parent.ArenaService)
local Profiles = require(script.Parent.Profiles)

local LeaderboardService = {}

local settings = Config.Leaderboard
local store: RobloxStore.OrderedStore
local buffer: LeaderboardBuffer.LeaderboardBuffer
local rows: { TextLabel } = {}
local status: TextLabel
local names: { [number]: string } = {}

local function nameOf(userId: number): string
	local cached = names[userId]
	if cached then
		return cached
	end
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(userId)
	local name: string? = if player then player.Name else nil
	if not name then
		local ok, result = pcall(function()
			return Players:GetNameFromUserIdAsync(userId)
		end)
		name = if ok then result else nil
	end
	-- Test players in Studio have negative ids with no account behind them.
	local resolved = name or ("Player " .. tostring(userId))
	names[userId] = resolved
	return resolved
end

local function label(parent: Instance, text: string, height: number, color: Color3): TextLabel
	local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	l.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, height)
	l.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
	l.TextScaled = true
	l.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	l.TextColor3 = color
	l.Text = text
	l.Parent = parent
	return l
end

local function buildBoard()
	local board = Instance.new("Part")
	board.Name = "Leaderboard"
	board.Anchored = true
	board.Size = Vector3.new(30, 18, 1)
	board.CFrame = ArenaService.boardCFrame()
	board.Color = Color3.fromRGB(24, 27, 36)
	board.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic

	local gui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
	gui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Back
	gui.LightInfluence = 0
	gui.SizingMode = Enum.SurfaceGuiSizingMode.PixelsPerStud
	gui.PixelsPerStud = 30
	gui.Parent = board

	local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	frame.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	frame.Parent = gui
	local padding = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	padding.PaddingTop = UDim.new(0, 24)
	padding.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 36)
	padding.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 36)
	padding.Parent = frame
	local layout = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
	layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 6)
	layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
	layout.Parent = frame

	local title = label(frame, "MOST WINS", 70, Color3.fromRGB(255, 196, 0))
	title.LayoutOrder = 0
	status = label(frame, "Loading...", 28, Color3.fromRGB(160, 166, 182))
	status.LayoutOrder = 1
	for i = 1, settings.Size do
		local row = label(frame, "", 36, Color3.fromRGB(240, 242, 247))
		row.LayoutOrder = i + 1
		rows[i] = row
	end

	local arena = Workspace:FindFirstChild("Arena")
	board.Parent = arena or Workspace
end

local function render(entries: { { key: string, value: number } })
	for i, row in rows do
		local entry = entries[i]
		if entry then
			local userId = tonumber(entry.key)
			local name = if userId then nameOf(userId) else entry.key
			row.Text =
				string.format("%d.  %s  —  %d win%s", i, name, entry.value, if entry.value == 1 then "" else "s")
		else
			row.Text = ""
		end
	end
	status.Text = if #entries == 0 then "No winners yet. Be the first!" else "All servers, refreshed regularly"
end

function LeaderboardService.refresh()
	local written, failed = buffer:flush()
	if failed > 0 then
		warn(string.format("[Leaderboard] %d of %d writes failed; retrying next refresh", failed, written + failed))
	end
	local ok, entries = store:top(settings.Size)
	if ok then
		render(entries)
	else
		warn("[Leaderboard] read failed: " .. tostring(entries))
	end
end

-- Writes what is queued; called on shutdown so the last round's wins land.
function LeaderboardService.flush()
	buffer:flush()
end

function LeaderboardService.start()
	local persistent
	store, persistent = RobloxStore.openOrdered(settings.StoreName)
	buffer = LeaderboardBuffer.new(store)
	-- The in-memory fallback has no request budget; refresh faster so the
	-- board is useful while playtesting in Studio.
	local interval = if persistent then settings.RefreshSeconds else 10
	buildBoard()

	Profiles.onChanged(function(player, data)
		buffer:record(player.UserId, data.wins)
	end)

	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			LeaderboardService.refresh()
			task.wait(interval)
		end
	end)
end

return LeaderboardService

--!strict
-- Status: experimental
-- Last verified: 2026-11-16
-- Test coverage: concurrent-allocation fixture in tests/TeleportHelper.spec.lua; Studio integration still required.
-- Experimental GUID routing migration pending second human review and Studio integration.
-- Intended use: example; choose DataStore or MemoryStore coordination for your matchmaking lifetime.
--[[
TeleportHelper.lua

Reserved-server allocation publishes a candidate through UpdateAsync and every
allocator uses the winning record. Teleport initiation and destination arrival
are tracked separately. A successful TeleportAsync call only means initiation;
the destination must call markReservedServerArrival().
]]

local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")

local ALLOCATION_LIFETIME_SECONDS = 60 * 60
local MAX_MATCH_ID_LENGTH = 20
local reservedServers = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("ReservedServerAllocations_v3")

export type TeleportData = { [string]: any }
export type AllocationState = "allocated" | "teleporting" | "arrived"
export type AllocationRecord = {
    allocationId: string,
    reservedServerId: string,
    placeId: number,
    matchId: string,
    state: AllocationState,
    createdAt: number,
    expiresAt: number,
    destinationJobId: string?,
}
export type ReservedTeleportState = "failed" | "allocated" | "teleport_started"
export type ReservedTeleportResult = {
    state: ReservedTeleportState,
    allocation: AllocationRecord?,
    error: any?,
}

local TeleportHelper = {}

local function allocationKey(placeId: number, matchId: string): string
    return `reserved_{placeId}_{matchId}`
end

local function validateReservedRequest(
    players: { Player },
    placeId: number,
    matchId: string
): string?
    if placeId ~= placeId or placeId == math.huge or placeId % 1 ~= 0 or placeId <= 0 then
        return "placeId must be a positive finite integer"
    end
    if matchId == "" or #matchId > MAX_MATCH_ID_LENGTH then
        return `matchId must contain 1-{MAX_MATCH_ID_LENGTH} bytes`
    end
    if #players == 0 or #players > 50 then
        return "reserved teleports require 1-50 players"
    end
    local seenUserIds: { [number]: boolean } = {}
    for _, player in players do
        if typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") or player.Parent ~= Players then
            return "every player must be a current Players member"
        end
        if seenUserIds[player.UserId] then
            return "players must not contain duplicates"
        end
        seenUserIds[player.UserId] = true
    end
    return nil
end

local function makeOptions(teleportData: TeleportData?): TeleportOptions
    local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
    if teleportData ~= nil then
        options:SetTeleportData(teleportData)
    end
    return options
end

local function teleport(
    players: { Player },
    placeId: number,
    options: TeleportOptions?
): (boolean, any?)
    local ok, response = pcall(function()
        return TeleportService:TeleportAsync(placeId, players, options)
    end)
    if not ok then
        warn("TeleportHelper: TeleportAsync failed:", tostring(response))
        return false, response
    end
    return true, response
end

local function isAllocation(value: any): boolean
    return type(value) == "table"
        and type(value.allocationId) == "string"
        and type(value.reservedServerId) == "string"
        and type(value.expiresAt) == "number"
end

local function freshAllocation(key: string): AllocationRecord?
    local getOptions = Instance.new("DataStoreGetOptions")
    getOptions.UseCache = false
    local ok, value = pcall(function()
        return reservedServers:GetAsync(key, getOptions)
    end)
    if ok and isAllocation(value) then
        return value :: AllocationRecord
    end
    return nil
end

function TeleportHelper._selectAllocation(
    current: any,
    candidate: AllocationRecord,
    now: number
): AllocationRecord
    if isAllocation(current) and (current :: AllocationRecord).expiresAt > now then
        return current :: AllocationRecord
    end
    return candidate
end

local function allocate(placeId: number, matchId: string): (AllocationRecord?, any?)
    local now = os.time()
    local candidate: AllocationRecord = {
        allocationId = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false),
        reservedServerId = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false),
        placeId = placeId,
        matchId = matchId,
        state = "allocated",
        createdAt = now,
        expiresAt = now + ALLOCATION_LIFETIME_SECONDS,
        destinationJobId = nil,
    }
    local key = allocationKey(placeId, matchId)
    local publishOk, winner = pcall(function()
        return reservedServers:UpdateAsync(key, function(current: any): AllocationRecord?
            return TeleportHelper._selectAllocation(current, candidate, now)
        end)
    end)
    if publishOk and isAllocation(winner) then
        return winner :: AllocationRecord, nil
    end

    -- UpdateAsync failures can be ambiguous. Read without cache and use the
    -- backend winner rather than reserving/publishing another ID.
    local reconciled = freshAllocation(key)
    if reconciled and reconciled.expiresAt > now then
        return reconciled, nil
    end
    return nil, winner
end

local function updateState(
    allocation: AllocationRecord,
    state: AllocationState,
    destinationJobId: string?
): (AllocationRecord?, any?)
    local key = allocationKey(allocation.placeId, allocation.matchId)
    local ok, updated = pcall(function()
        return reservedServers:UpdateAsync(key, function(current: any): AllocationRecord?
            if not isAllocation(current) then
                return nil
            end
            local record = current :: AllocationRecord
            if record.allocationId ~= allocation.allocationId then
                return nil
            end
            record.state = state
            record.destinationJobId = destinationJobId
            return record
        end)
    end)
    if ok and isAllocation(updated) then
        return updated :: AllocationRecord, nil
    end

    local reconciled = freshAllocation(key)
    if
        reconciled
        and reconciled.allocationId == allocation.allocationId
        and reconciled.state == state
    then
        return reconciled, nil
    end
    return nil, updated
end

function TeleportHelper.teleportToPlace(
    player: Player,
    placeId: number,
    teleportData: TeleportData?
): boolean
    local optionsOk, options = pcall(makeOptions, teleportData)
    if not optionsOk then
        warn("TeleportHelper: invalid teleport data:", tostring(options))
        return false
    end
    local ok = teleport({ player }, placeId, options)
    return ok
end

function TeleportHelper.teleportToServer(
    player: Player,
    placeId: number,
    jobId: string,
    teleportData: TeleportData?
): boolean
    local optionsOk, options = pcall(makeOptions, teleportData)
    if not optionsOk then
        warn("TeleportHelper: invalid teleport data:", tostring(options))
        return false
    end
    options.ServerInstanceId = jobId
    local ok = teleport({ player }, placeId, options)
    return ok
end

function TeleportHelper.teleportToReservedServer(
    players: { Player },
    placeId: number,
    matchId: string,
    teleportData: TeleportData?
): (boolean, ReservedTeleportResult)
    local validationError = validateReservedRequest(players, placeId, matchId)
    if validationError then
        return false, { state = "failed", allocation = nil, error = validationError }
    end

    local allocation, allocationError = allocate(placeId, matchId)
    if not allocation then
        return false, { state = "failed", allocation = nil, error = allocationError }
    end

    local trackingRecord, trackingError = updateState(allocation, "teleporting", nil)
    if not trackingRecord then
        return false, { state = "allocated", allocation = allocation, error = trackingError }
    end

    local data: TeleportData = {}
    if teleportData then
        for key, value in teleportData do
            data[key] = value
        end
    end
    data.reservedAllocationId = trackingRecord.allocationId
    data.reservedMatchId = matchId

    local optionsOk, options = pcall(makeOptions, data)
    if not optionsOk then
        return false, { state = "allocated", allocation = trackingRecord, error = options }
    end
    options.ReservedServerId = trackingRecord.reservedServerId
    local started, teleportError = teleport(players, placeId, options)
    if not started then
        return false, { state = "allocated", allocation = trackingRecord, error = teleportError }
    end
    return true, { state = "teleport_started", allocation = trackingRecord, error = nil }
end

function TeleportHelper.markReservedServerArrival(
    placeId: number,
    matchId: string,
    allocationId: string
): (boolean, AllocationRecord?)
    local current = freshAllocation(allocationKey(placeId, matchId))
    if not current or current.allocationId ~= allocationId then
        return false, nil
    end
    local updated = updateState(current, "arrived", game.JobId)
    return updated ~= nil, updated
end

return TeleportHelper

-- ShieldService: the laser shield around each safehouse. When a player
-- activates it, the shell turns visible and solid for 26 seconds, and no
-- rival can walk in to steal. After it ends, a 48 second cooldown runs —
-- counted from the moment the shield ends, not from activation — so a full
-- cycle is 74 seconds. The shell's solidity always matches its visibility:
-- a transparent shell must never be solid, or the collision groups below
-- would block players the shield is supposed to let through.

local PhysicsService = game:GetService("PhysicsService")
local BrainrotData = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Shared.BrainrotData)

local ShieldService = {}

-- player -> { endsAt, readyAgainAt } in os.clock() seconds.
local shields = {}

local function setShell(base, visible)
	local shell = base.shell
	if not shell then
		return
	end
	-- Visibility and solidity are set together, always. This is the rule
	-- that makes the collision groups below actually matter.
	shell.Transparency = visible and 0.5 or 1
	shell.CanCollide = visible
end

function ShieldService.init(ctx)
	local world = ctx.world
	local events = ctx.events
	local remotes = ctx.remotes

	-- Thirteen collision groups. The shield only ever blocks people: it
	-- collides with Players and with carried brainrots, and with nothing
	-- else, so it never stops a character being placed or a decoration
	-- from sitting where it belongs.
	for _, name in ipairs(BrainrotData.CollisionGroups) do
		pcall(function()
			PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup(name)
		end)
	end
	for _, other in ipairs(BrainrotData.CollisionGroups) do
		if other ~= "Shield" then
			local blocks = (other == "Players") or (other == "Carry")
			pcall(function()
				PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable("Shield", other, blocks)
			end)
		end
	end

	local function baseOf(player)
		local baseService = ctx.services.BaseService
		local index = baseService.getBaseIndex(player)
		if not index then
			return nil
		end
		return world.bases[index]
	end

	remotes.ShieldActivate.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
		local base = baseOf(player)
		if not base then
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Claim a base first!")
			return
		end
		local now = os.clock()
		local record = shields[player]
		if record and now < record.readyAgainAt then
			local left = math.ceil(record.readyAgainAt - now)
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Shield cooling down: " .. tostring(left) .. "s left.")
			return
		end
		-- endsAt is activation plus 26; readyAgainAt is endsAt plus 48.
		local endsAt = now + BrainrotData.Shield.duration
		local readyAgainAt = endsAt + BrainrotData.Shield.cooldown
		shields[player] = { endsAt = endsAt, readyAgainAt = readyAgainAt }
		setShell(base, true)
		events.ShieldChanged:Fire(player, true)
		remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Shield up for 26 seconds!")
	end)

	-- Watcher: hide every shield the moment its 26 seconds are over.
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(0.5)
			local now = os.clock()
			for player, record in pairs(shields) do
				if now >= record.endsAt then
					local base = baseOf(player)
					if base then
						setShell(base, false)
					end
					shields[player] = { endsAt = 0, readyAgainAt = record.readyAgainAt }
					events.ShieldChanged:Fire(player, false)
				end
			end
		end
	end)
end

function ShieldService.isShieldActive(player)
	local record = shields[player]
	if not record then
		return false
	end
	return os.clock() < record.endsAt
end

function ShieldService.isShieldReady(player)
	local record = shields[player]
	if not record then
		return true
	end
	return os.clock() >= record.readyAgainAt
end

return ShieldService

--!strict

-- Cooldown type
-- by @vuppyan

local Core = require("../Core")
type Map<K, V> = Core.Map<K, V>
type Supplier<T> = Core.Supplier<T>

local Duration = require("./Duration")
type Duration = Duration.Duration

local fail = Core.Errors.errorWithScope("Cooldown")

--[=[
    A mutable, keyed cooldown timer for measuring the time between uses of
    something.

    A `Cooldown` holds one entry per key, as server-side scripts often need a
    separate timer per player or ability. Every method that takes a `key`
    parameter acts on that key's entry, and a single global timer can be
    implemented by using a constant key. Keys cannot be `nil` or NaN.

    Each entry has up to the `Cooldown`'s maximum number of charges. A use
    spends a charge, and spent charges recharge one at a time, each taking the
    `Cooldown`'s length. A key with no entry has all of its charges available:
    an entry is created when a charge is spent, and removed once all of its
    charges have recharged.

    Due to how server-client authority works, client-side `Cooldown`s only
    affect visuals, and `tryUse` on the server-side is the real check to run.

    Unlike `Duration`s, `Cooldown`s are not frozen, and their methods modify
    them in place.

    Supports `tostring()`.

    Error messages thrown by `Cooldown` functions are prefixed with the function
    that threw them, such as `[Cooldown.tryUse()]: `, after the usual position
    prefix added by `error()`.

    ```lua
    local fireballCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(5))

    castRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
        if fireballCd:tryUse(player) then
            castFireball(player)
        end
    end)

    Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
        fireballCd:reset(player) -- free the player's entry
    end)
    ```

    @tag mutable
    @class Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
]=]
local Cooldown = {}
Cooldown.__index = Cooldown

type CooldownEntry = {
    -- both are clock readings
    startedAt: number,
    readyAt: number,
    charges: number,
}

--[=[
    Options for `Cooldown.new`.

    Common choices for `clock` are:
    * `os.clock` for local elapsed time (the default)
    * `os.time` for Unix seconds with whole-second precision
    * `function() return workspace:GetServerTimeNow() end` for time synchronized
      between client and server

    @interface CooldownOptions
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @field clock Supplier<number>? -- The clock function to use, which returns the current time in seconds and should not go backwards (defaults to `os.clock`)
    @field maxCharges number? -- The maximum number of charges each entry can hold (defaults to 1)
]=]
export type CooldownOptions = {
    read clock: Supplier<number>?,
    read maxCharges: number?,
}

type CooldownData<K> = {
    read _clock: Supplier<number>,
    _length: number,
    _maxCharges: number,
    _entries: Map<K, CooldownEntry>,
}

export type Cooldown<K> = typeof(setmetatable({} :: CooldownData<K>, Cooldown))

-- Helper to bring `key`'s entry up to date at time `now`, adding every charge
-- that finished recharging since it was last touched. Deletes the entry and
-- returns nil once all charges are back.
local function settle<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K, now: number): CooldownEntry?
    local entry = self._entries[key]
    if entry == nil or now < entry.readyAt then
        return entry
    end

    -- the charge in progress finished at readyAt, and each later charge took
    -- the default length after that
    local interval = self._length
    local recovered = 1
    if interval == 0 then
        recovered = self._maxCharges
    else
        recovered += math.floor((now - entry.readyAt) / interval)
    end

    entry.charges += recovered
    if entry.charges >= self._maxCharges then
        self._entries[key] = nil
        return nil
    end

    -- the next charge began when the last recovered one finished
    -- skip the multiplication when nothing extra was recovered,
    -- since 0 * inf is NaN
    if recovered > 1 then
        entry.startedAt = entry.readyAt + (recovered - 1) * interval
    else
        entry.startedAt = entry.readyAt
    end
    entry.readyAt = entry.startedAt + interval
    return entry
end

--[=[
    Creates a new `Cooldown` with the given length and options.

    The clock function should return the current time in seconds, and should not
    go backwards. Common choices are:
    * `os.clock` for local elapsed time (the default)
    * `os.time` for Unix seconds with whole-second precision
    * `function() return workspace:GetServerTimeNow() end` for time synchronized
      between client and server

    > **Note: pass the key type with `Cooldown.new<<K>>(...)`**
    >
    > Luau cannot infer the key type `K` from this constructor's arguments, so
    > write it explicitly, as in the example. Without it:
    > * `K` becomes `unknown`, so keys are not type checked, and the result
    >   cannot be assigned to a `Cooldown<Player>` annotation.
    > * In Studio and the editor, passing an options table that leaves out any
    >   option, such as `{ maxCharges = 2 }`, is a type error, due to a Luau
    >   type checker bug.

    ```lua
    local dashCd = Cooldown.new<<Player>>(
        Duration.fromSeconds(3),
        { maxCharges = 2 }
    )
    local synced = Cooldown.new<<string>>(Duration.SECOND, {
        clock = function()
            return workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
        end,
    })
    ```

    @since v0.1.3
    @param length Duration -- The time each charge takes to recharge
    @param options CooldownOptions? -- The options to use (defaults to `{ clock = os.clock, maxCharges = 1 }`)
    @return Cooldown<K> -- The new `Cooldown`
    @error "[Cooldown.new()]: Length cannot be negative" -- Thrown if `length` is negative
    @error "[Cooldown.new()]: Max charges must be a positive integer" -- Thrown if `options.maxCharges` is not a positive integer
]=]
function Cooldown.new<K>(length: Duration, options: CooldownOptions?): Cooldown<K>
    local clock = options and options.clock or os.clock
    local maxCharges = options and options.maxCharges or 1

    if length:isNegative() then
        fail("Length cannot be negative")
    elseif maxCharges < 1 or maxCharges % 1 ~= 0 then
        fail("Max charges must be a positive integer")
    end

    return setmetatable({
        _clock = clock,
        _length = length:toSeconds(),
        _maxCharges = maxCharges,
        _entries = {},
    }, Cooldown)
end

--[=[
    Attempts to spend a charge from the given key's entry, returning `true` if a
    charge was available, or `false` if none were and nothing happened.

    An optional `length` parameter can be given to override the `Cooldown`'s
    length for this one use. This may be useful for special cases like a longer
    cooldown after a charged attack. An override only applies if this use starts
    a recharge, which happens when the entry had all of its charges. If a charge
    is already recharging, the use only spends a charge, and the timer already
    running isn't changed.

    Zero-length uses still require a charge to be available, but succeed without
    spending it.

    ```lua
    local dashCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(3), { maxCharges = 2 })
    dashCd:tryUse(player) -- true, 1 charge left, and a charge starts recharging
    dashCd:tryUse(player) -- true, 0 charges left
    dashCd:tryUse(player) -- false
    -- 3 seconds later
    dashCd:tryUse(player) -- true, the first charge recharged

    local attack = Cooldown.new(Duration.SECOND)
    attack:tryUse(player, Duration.fromSeconds(4)) -- true, ready in 4 seconds
    ```

    @method tryUse
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @param length Duration? -- The custom length to use (defaults to the `Cooldown`'s length)
    @return boolean -- Whether a charge was available
    @error "[Cooldown.tryUse()]: Key cannot be nil or NaN" -- Thrown if `key` is `nil` or NaN
    @error "[Cooldown.tryUse()]: Length cannot be negative" -- Thrown if `length` is negative
]=]
function Cooldown.tryUse<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K, length: Duration?): boolean
    if key == nil or key ~= key then
        fail("Key cannot be nil or NaN")
    elseif length and length:isNegative() then
        fail("Length cannot be negative")
    end

    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    local available = if entry then entry.charges else self._maxCharges
    if available < 1 then
        return false
    end

    local seconds = if length then length:toSeconds() else self._length
    if seconds == 0 then
        return true -- zero-length uses never start a cooldown
    end

    if entry == nil then
        -- first use from full: this charge starts recharging now
        self._entries[key] = {
            charges = self._maxCharges - 1,
            startedAt = now,
            readyAt = now + seconds,
        }
    else
        -- a charge is already recharging: spend one and leave the timer alone
        entry.charges -= 1
    end
    return true
end

--[=[
    Starts a recharge for the given key's entry without checking, setting its
    available charges to 0 and replacing any recharge already in progress.

    This method may be useful for effects like silences or stuns.

    An optional `length` parameter can be given to override the `Cooldown`'s
    length for the first charge. This may be useful for special cases like a
    longer cooldown after a charged attack. Any later charges recharge with the
    `Cooldown`'s length.

    A length of zero removes the entry instead, restoring all of its charges
    like [Cooldown:reset].

    ```lua
    local abilityCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(5), { maxCharges = 3 })
    abilityCd:start(player, Duration.fromSeconds(2)) -- stunned, 0 charges
    -- 2 seconds later
    abilityCd:charges(player) -- 1
    -- 5 seconds later
    abilityCd:charges(player) -- 2
    ```

    @method start
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @param length Duration? -- The custom length to use (defaults to the `Cooldown`'s length)
    @error "[Cooldown.start()]: Key cannot be nil or NaN" -- Thrown if `key` is `nil` or NaN
    @error "[Cooldown.start()]: Length cannot be negative" -- Thrown if `length` is negative
]=]
function Cooldown.start<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K, length: Duration?): ()
    if key == nil or key ~= key then
        fail("Key cannot be nil or NaN")
    elseif length and length:isNegative() then
        fail("Length cannot be negative")
    end
    local seconds = if length then length:toSeconds() else self._length
    if seconds == 0 then
        self._entries[key] = nil
        return
    end
    local now = self._clock()
    self._entries[key] = {
        charges = 0,
        startedAt = now,
        readyAt = now + seconds,
    }
end

--[=[
    Shifts the time the given key's charge in progress finishes by a signed
    `Duration`, doing nothing if the key has no entry (all of its charges are
    available).

    Negative `Duration`s shorten the recharge, while positive `Duration`s
    lengthen it. If a negative `Duration` is larger than the time remaining, the
    charge finishes, and the leftover time carries over to the following
    charges.

    ```lua
    local abilityCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(10), { maxCharges = 2 })
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    abilityCd:tryUse(player) -- 0 charges, next charge in 10 seconds
    abilityCd:adjust(player, Duration.fromSeconds(-4)) -- next charge in 6 seconds
    abilityCd:adjust(player, Duration.fromSeconds(-8))
    -- 1 charge, and the next charge is 2 seconds in, so it's ready in 8 seconds
    ```

    @method adjust
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @param delta Duration -- The amount to adjust
    @error "[Cooldown.adjust()]: Key cannot be nil or NaN" -- Thrown if `key` is `nil` or NaN
]=]
function Cooldown.adjust<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K, delta: Duration): ()
    if key == nil or key ~= key then
        fail("Key cannot be nil or NaN")
    end

    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    if entry == nil then
        return
    end

    entry.readyAt += delta:toSeconds()
    settle(self, key, now)
end

--[=[
    Removes the given key's entry, restoring all of its charges.

    @method reset
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @error "[Cooldown.reset()]: Key cannot be nil or NaN" -- Thrown if `key` is `nil` or NaN
]=]
function Cooldown.reset<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): ()
    if key == nil or key ~= key then
        fail("Key cannot be nil or NaN")
    end
    self._entries[key] = nil
end

--[=[
    Removes every entry, restoring all charges for every key.

    @method resetAll
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
]=]
function Cooldown.resetAll<K>(self: Cooldown<K>): ()
    self._entries = {}
end

--[=[
    Brings every entry up to date, removing the entries whose charges have all
    recharged.

    Entries are otherwise only removed when their key is accessed, so this
    method may be useful for freeing memory from keys that are no longer used.

    @method prune
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @return number -- The number of entries remaining after pruning
]=]
function Cooldown.prune<K>(self: Cooldown<K>): number
    local now = self._clock()
    local total = 0
    for key in self._entries do
        local entry = settle(self, key, now)
        if entry ~= nil then
            total += 1
        end
    end
    return total
end

--[=[
    Returns whether the given key has at least one charge available.

    This method should be used for display or branching. To check and spend a
    charge in one step, use [Cooldown:tryUse].

    @method isReady
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @return boolean -- Whether a charge is available
]=]
function Cooldown.isReady<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): boolean
    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    return entry == nil or entry.charges > 0
end

--[=[
    Returns the time remaining until the given key's charge in progress
    finishes, or [Duration.ZERO] if the key has no entry.

    With multiple charges, a nonzero return value does not mean the key is
    unready, as other charges may still be available. Use [Cooldown:isReady] to
    check readiness, or [Cooldown:remainingUntilFull] to check all charges at
    once.

    ```lua
    local abilityCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(10), { maxCharges = 3 })
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    -- 4 seconds later
    abilityCd:remaining(player) -- 6 seconds
    abilityCd:remainingUntilFull(player) -- 16 seconds
    abilityCd:isReady(player) -- true, since 1 charge is available
    ```

    @method remaining
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @return Duration -- The remaining time
]=]
function Cooldown.remaining<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): Duration
    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    return if entry
        then Duration.fromSeconds(entry.readyAt - now)
        else Duration.ZERO
end

--[=[
    Returns the progress of the given key's charge in progress in a range from
    0.0 to 1.0, or 1.0 if the key has no entry.

    With multiple charges, a return value below 1.0 does not mean the key is
    unready, as other charges may still be available. Use [Cooldown:isReady] to
    check readiness, or [Cooldown:progressUntilFull] to check all charges at
    once.

    ```lua
    local abilityCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(10), { maxCharges = 3 })
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    -- 4 seconds later
    abilityCd:progress(player) -- 0.4
    abilityCd:progressUntilFull(player) -- 0.4666..., (1 + 0.4) / 3 charges
    ```

    @method progress
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @return number -- The progress
]=]
function Cooldown.progress<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): number
    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    if entry == nil then
        return 1
    end
    local interval = entry.readyAt - entry.startedAt
    return math.clamp((now - entry.startedAt) / interval, 0, 1)
end

--[=[
    Returns the time remaining until all of the given key's charges have
    recharged.

    A return value of [Duration.ZERO] indicates that all charges are available.
    Charges after the one in progress are assumed to take the `Cooldown`'s
    current length. To check the time remaining on the charge in progress, use
    [Cooldown:remaining].

    @method remainingUntilFull
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @return Duration -- The remaining time
]=]
function Cooldown.remainingUntilFull<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): Duration
    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    if entry == nil then
        return Duration.ZERO
    end
    local missing = self._maxCharges - entry.charges
    local seconds = entry.readyAt - now
    if missing > 1 then
        seconds += (missing - 1) * self._length
    end
    return Duration.fromSeconds(seconds):max(Duration.ZERO)
end

--[=[
    Returns the progress towards all of the given key's charges being available
    in a range from 0.0 to 1.0, counting the charge in progress as a fraction.

    A return value of 1.0 indicates that all charges are available. To check the
    progress of the charge in progress, use [Cooldown:progress].

    @method progressUntilFull
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @return number -- The progress
]=]
function Cooldown.progressUntilFull<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): number
    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    if entry == nil then
        return 1
    end
    local interval = entry.readyAt - entry.startedAt
    local partial = math.clamp((now - entry.startedAt) / interval, 0, 1)
    return (entry.charges + partial) / self._maxCharges
end

--[=[
    Returns the `Cooldown`'s length, the time each charge takes to recharge.

    @method getLength
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @return Duration -- The length
]=]
function Cooldown.getLength<K>(self: Cooldown<K>): Duration
    return Duration.fromSeconds(self._length)
end

--[=[
    Sets the `Cooldown`'s length, the time each charge takes to recharge.

    Charges already in progress keep their current timers, and the new length
    applies to every charge that starts recharging afterwards.

    ```lua
    local abilityCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(10), { maxCharges = 2 })
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    abilityCd:tryUse(player)
    abilityCd:setLength(Duration.fromSeconds(4))
    abilityCd:remaining(player) -- 10 seconds, the charge in progress is unchanged
    -- 10 seconds later
    abilityCd:remaining(player) -- 4 seconds, the next charge uses the new length
    ```

    @method setLength
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param length Duration -- The length
    @error "[Cooldown.setLength()]: Length cannot be negative" -- Thrown if `length` is negative
]=]
function Cooldown.setLength<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, length: Duration): ()
    if length:isNegative() then
        fail("Length cannot be negative")
    end
    self._length = length:toSeconds()
end

--[=[
    Returns the number of charges available for the given key.

    @method charges
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @param key K -- The key of the entry
    @return number -- The number of charges
]=]
function Cooldown.charges<K>(self: Cooldown<K>, key: K): number
    local now = self._clock()
    local entry = settle(self, key, now)
    return if entry then entry.charges else self._maxCharges
end

--[=[
    Returns the maximum number of charges each entry can hold.

    @method maxCharges
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @return number -- The maximum number of charges
]=]
function Cooldown.maxCharges<K>(self: Cooldown<K>): number
    return self._maxCharges
end

--[=[
    Returns whether the given value is a `Cooldown`.

    Only values created by `Cooldown` functions are considered `Cooldown`s;
    tables with the same fields are not.

    @since v0.1.3
    @param value any -- The value to check
    @return boolean -- Whether `value` is a `Cooldown`
]=]
function Cooldown.is(value: any): boolean
    return getmetatable(value) == Cooldown
end

--[=[
    Returns a string representation of the `Cooldown`, including its length and
    number of entries.

    This method prunes the `Cooldown` (see [Cooldown:prune]) to count only the
    entries with charges still recharging.

    Also used by `tostring()`.

    ```lua
    local fireballCd = Cooldown.new(Duration.fromSeconds(5))
    fireballCd:tryUse("a")
    fireballCd:tryUse("b")
    fireballCd:toString() -- "Cooldown(5s, 2 active)"
    -- 5 seconds later
    tostring(fireballCd) -- "Cooldown(5s, 0 active)"
    ```

    @method toString
    @within Cooldown
    @since v0.1.3
    @return string -- The string representation
]=]
function Cooldown.toString<K>(self: Cooldown<K>): string
    local active = self:prune()
    return string.format(
        "Cooldown(%s, %d active)",
        Duration.fromSeconds(self._length):toHumanString(),
        active
    )
end
Cooldown.__tostring = Cooldown.toString

return Core.Class.sealed(Cooldown)

--!strict
-- Ties DataService to live players: loading on join, leaderstats, pushing
-- the profile to the owning client, saving on leave and on shutdown.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local DataService = require(script.Parent.Parent.Data.DataService)
local PlayerData = require(script.Parent.Parent.Data.PlayerData)

local ProfileRemote = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.Profile :: RemoteEvent

local Profiles = {}

local service: DataService.DataService
local changedCallbacks: { (Player, PlayerData.Data) -> () } = {}

function Profiles.init(dataService: DataService.DataService)
	service = dataService
end

function Profiles.onChanged(callback: (Player, PlayerData.Data) -> ())
	table.insert(changedCallbacks, callback)
end

function Profiles.isLoaded(player: Player): boolean
	return service:isLoaded(player.UserId)
end

function Profiles.get(player: Player): PlayerData.Data?
	return service:get(player.UserId)
end

local function syncLeaderstats(player: Player, data: PlayerData.Data)
	local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if not stats then
		local folder = Instance.new("Folder")
		folder.Name = "leaderstats"
		local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
		coins.Name = "Coins"
		coins.Parent = folder
		local wins = Instance.new("IntValue")
		wins.Name = "Wins"
		wins.Parent = folder
		folder.Parent = player
		stats = folder
	end
	assert(stats, "leaderstats folder missing")
	local coinsValue = stats:FindFirstChild("Coins") :: IntValue
	local winsValue = stats:FindFirstChild("Wins") :: IntValue
	coinsValue.Value = data.coins
	winsValue.Value = data.wins
end

function Profiles.push(player: Player)
	local data = Profiles.get(player)
	if not data then
		return
	end
	syncLeaderstats(player, data)
	ProfileRemote:FireClient(player, {
		coins = data.coins,
		wins = data.wins,
		bestWave = data.bestWave,
		ownedTrails = table.clone(data.ownedTrails),
		equippedTrail = data.equippedTrail,
	})
	for _, callback in changedCallbacks do
		task.spawn(callback, player, data)
	end
end

-- Mutates the player's data in place and tells everyone who cares. The
-- change is persisted by the next autosave or when the player leaves.
function Profiles.mutate(player: Player, mutator: (PlayerData.Data) -> ()): boolean
	local data = Profiles.get(player)
	if not data then
		return false
	end
	mutator(data)
	Profiles.push(player)
	return true
end

function Profiles.load(player: Player): boolean
	local ok, result = service:load(player.UserId)
	if not ok then
		warn(string.format("[Data] load failed for %s: %s", player.Name, tostring(result)))
		player:Kick(tostring(result))
		return false
	end
	if player.Parent ~= Players then
		-- Left while we were loading. Release the lock right away.
		service:unload(player.UserId)
		return false
	end
	Profiles.push(player)
	return true
end

function Profiles.release(player: Player)
	local ok, err = service:unload(player.UserId)
	-- "not loaded": never loaded, or shutdown is already releasing it.
	if not ok and err ~= "not loaded" then
		warn(string.format("[Data] save on leave failed for %s: %s", player.Name, tostring(err)))
	end
end

local function kickIfLost(userId: number, err: string?)
	if err == "session lost" then
		local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(userId)
		if player then
			player:Kick("Your data was opened on another server. Please rejoin.")
		end
	end
end

function Profiles.saveAll(release: boolean)
	local pending = 0
	for _, userId in service:userIds() do
		pending += 1
		task.spawn(function()
			local ok, err
			if release then
				ok, err = service:unload(userId)
			else
				ok, err = service:save(userId, false)
			end
			if not ok and err ~= "not loaded" then
				warn(string.format("[Data] save failed for %d: %s", userId, tostring(err)))
				kickIfLost(userId, err)
			end
			pending -= 1
		end)
	end
	-- BindToClose gives the server 30 seconds in total.
	local deadline = os.clock() + 25
	while pending > 0 and os.clock() < deadline do
		task.wait(0.1)
	end
end

return Profiles

--!strict
-- Status: experimental
-- Last verified: 2026-06-17
-- Test coverage: no automated coverage
-- Intended use: example; adapt and test before production.

--[[
    DebugDraw.lua
    Utility for drawing temporary debug visuals in the 3D world.

    Usage:
        local DebugDraw = require(path.to.DebugDraw)
        DebugDraw.point(workspace, Vector3.new(0, 10, 0), Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0), 2)
        DebugDraw.ray(workspace, origin, direction, Color3.fromRGB(0, 255, 0), 2)
        DebugDraw.box(workspace, cframe, size, Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255), 2)

        DebugDraw.clear() -- removes all tracked debug parts
]]

local DebugDraw = {}

local registry = {}

local function validateParent(parent)
    assert(typeof(parent) == "Instance", "parent must be an Instance")
end

local function createBase()
    local part = Instance.new("Part")
    part.Anchored = true
    part.CanCollide = false
    part.CanQuery = false
    part.CanTouch = false
    part.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
    return part
end

local function track(part, lifetime)
    table.insert(registry, part)

    if lifetime then
        task.delay(lifetime, function()
            if part.Parent ~= nil then
                part:Destroy()
            end
            for i = #registry, 1, -1 do
                if registry[i] == part then
                    table.remove(registry, i)
                    break
                end
            end
        end)
    end
end

function DebugDraw.point(parent, position, color, lifetime)
    validateParent(parent)
    local part = createBase()
    part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
    part.Size = Vector3.new(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
    part.CFrame = CFrame.new(position)
    part.Color = color or Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0)
    part.Parent = parent
    track(part, lifetime)
    return part
end

function DebugDraw.ray(parent, origin, direction, color, lifetime)
    validateParent(parent)
    local distance = direction.Magnitude
    assert(distance > 0, "direction must be non-zero")

    local part = createBase()
    part.Size = Vector3.new(0.1, 0.1, distance)
    part.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(origin, origin + direction) * CFrame.new(0, 0, -distance / 2)
    part.Color = color or Color3.fromRGB(0, 255, 0)
    part.Parent = parent
    track(part, lifetime)
    return part
end

function DebugDraw.box(parent, cframe, size, color, lifetime)
    validateParent(parent)
    local part = createBase()
    part.Size = size
    part.CFrame = cframe
    part.Transparency = 0.7
    part.Color = color or Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 255)
    part.Parent = parent
    track(part, lifetime)
    return part
end

function DebugDraw.clear()
    for i = #registry, 1, -1 do
        local part = registry[i]
        if part and part.Parent ~= nil then
            part:Destroy()
        end
        registry[i] = nil
    end
end

return DebugDraw

-- StealService: the steal in steal-a-brainrot. Clicking a character on
-- someone else's stand — while their shield is down — picks it up and
-- welds it in front of you. Walk it home and click your own base platform
-- to place it on a free stand: the steal succeeds. If you die, leave, or
-- have no free stand, the character goes straight back to its owner's
-- stand. Clicking your own character sells it for half price instead.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local BrainrotData = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Shared.BrainrotData)

local StealService = {}

-- model -> { owner, slot, entry, mutationId } for every placed character.
local placed = {}
-- player -> { model, victim, slot, entry, mutationId } while carrying.
local carrying = {}

local function setModelAnchored(model, anchored)
	for _, part in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if part:IsA("BasePart") then
			part.Anchored = anchored
			part.CanCollide = false
		end
	end
end

function StealService.init(ctx)
	local world = ctx.world
	local events = ctx.events
	local remotes = ctx.remotes
	local baseService = ctx.services.BaseService
	local shieldService = ctx.services.ShieldService

	local function returnToOwner(record)
		if not record then
			return
		end
		local victim = record.owner
		local baseIndex = baseService.getBaseIndex(victim)
		if baseIndex then
			local base = world.bases[baseIndex]
			local padPos = base.pads[record.slot]
			if padPos and record.model and record.model.Parent then
				setModelAnchored(record.model, true)
				record.model.Parent = base.model
				record.model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(padPos + Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0)))
				return
			end
		end
		if record.model then
			record.model:Destroy()
		end
	end

	local function stopCarrying(player, restore)
		local record = carrying[player]
		if not record then
			return
		end
		carrying[player] = nil
		local flag = player:FindFirstChild("Carrying")
		if flag then
			flag.Value = false
		end
		local character = player.Character
		if character then
			local weld = character:FindFirstChild("CarryWeld")
			if weld then
				weld:Destroy()
			end
		end
		if restore then
			returnToOwner(record)
		end
	end

	-- When a character lands on a stand, give it a click handler: the
	-- owner sells it, anyone else tries to steal it.
	events.CharacterPlaced.Event:Connect(function(player, slot, model, entry, mutationId)
		placed[model] = { owner = player, slot = slot, entry = entry, mutationId = mutationId }
		local detector = Instance.new("ClickDetector")
		detector.MaxActivationDistance = 32
		detector.Parent = model
		detector.MouseClick:Connect(function(clicker)
			local info = placed[model]
			if not info then
				return
			end
			if clicker == info.owner then
				events.SellRequested:Fire(clicker, info.slot)
				placed[model] = nil
				return
			end
			if carrying[clicker] then
				remotes.Notify:FireClient(clicker, "You are already carrying a brainrot!")
				return
			end
			if shieldService.isShieldActive(info.owner) then
				remotes.Notify:FireClient(clicker, info.owner.Name .. "'s shield is up! Come back later.")
				return
			end
			-- Pick it up: unanchor, weld it in front of the carrier.
			local character = clicker.Character
			local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
			if not root then
				return
			end
			setModelAnchored(model, false)
			local weld = Instance.new("Weld")
			weld.Name = "CarryWeld"
			weld.Part0 = root
			weld.Part1 = model.PrimaryPart
			weld.C0 = CFrame.new(0, 0, -2.5)
			weld.Parent = character
			model.Parent = character
			placed[model] = nil
			carrying[clicker] = { model = model, victim = info.owner, slot = info.slot, entry = info.entry, mutationId = info.mutationId }
			local flag = clicker:FindFirstChild("Carrying")
			if not flag then
				flag = Instance.new("BoolValue")
				flag.Name = "Carrying"
				flag.Parent = clicker
			end
			flag.Value = true
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(clicker, "You stole " .. info.entry.name .. "! Carry it home to your base.")
			remotes.Notify:FireClient(info.owner, clicker.Name .. " is stealing your " .. info.entry.name .. "!")
		end)
	end)

	-- Clicking your own base platform while carrying places the stolen
	-- character on your first free stand. No free stand: it goes back.
	for _, base in ipairs(world.bases) do
		local platform = base.model:FindFirstChild("Platform")
		if platform then
			local detector = Instance.new("ClickDetector")
			detector.MaxActivationDistance = 40
			detector.Parent = platform
			detector.MouseClick:Connect(function(clicker)
				local record = carrying[clicker]
				if not record then
					return
				end
				local myIndex = baseService.getBaseIndex(clicker)
				if myIndex ~= base.index then
					remotes.Notify:FireClient(clicker, "That is not your base!")
					return
				end
				if not baseService.hasFreeStand(clicker) then
					remotes.Notify:FireClient(clicker, "No free stand! The brainrot escapes back.")
					stopCarrying(clicker, true)
					return
				end
				-- Place it on the first free stand of the carrier's base.
				local count = baseService.getStandCount(clicker)
				local slot = nil
				for i = 1, count do
					if baseService.getSlot(clicker, i) == nil then
						slot = i
						break
					end
				end
				if slot == nil then
					stopCarrying(clicker, true)
					return
				end
				local model = record.model
				local character = clicker.Character
				if character then
					local weld = character:FindFirstChild("CarryWeld")
					if weld then
						weld:Destroy()
					end
				end
				local flag = clicker:FindFirstChild("Carrying")
				if flag then
					flag.Value = false
				end
				carrying[clicker] = nil
				local padPos = base.pads[slot]
				setModelAnchored(model, true)
				model.Parent = base.model
				model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(padPos + Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0)))
				events.CharacterPlaced:Fire(clicker, slot, model, record.entry, record.mutationId)
				remotes.Notify:FireClient(clicker, "Stolen! " .. record.entry.name .. " is yours now.")
				remotes.Notify:FireClient(record.victim, clicker.Name .. " stole your " .. record.entry.name .. "!")
			end)
		end
	end

	-- If the carrier dies or leaves, the brainrot goes home.
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		stopCarrying(player, true)
	end)
	local function watchCharacter(player)
		player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
			local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid", 5)
			if humanoid then
				humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
					stopCarrying(player, true)
				end)
			end
		end)
	end
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(watchCharacter)
	for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
		watchCharacter(player)
	end

	-- The menu's sell grid: selling a stand by number. The server checks
	-- the slot really holds one of the caller's own characters before it
	-- pays out, so a client cannot sell someone else's brainrot.
	remotes.SellCharacter.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, slot)
		if typeof(slot) ~= "number" then
			return
		end
		for model, info in pairs(placed) do
			if info.owner == player and info.slot == slot then
				events.SellRequested:Fire(player, slot)
				placed[model] = nil
				return
			end
		end
		remotes.Notify:FireClient(player, "Nothing to sell on stand " .. tostring(slot) .. ".")
	end)

	-- A sold character is no longer tracked as placed.
	events.CharacterRemoved.Event:Connect(function(_player, _slot)
		-- The model was destroyed by the seller, so nothing to clean up
		-- here; the placed map is cleared by the click handler.
	end)

	-- A bat hit interrupts a carry: the thief drops the brainrot and it
	-- goes straight back to its owner's stand, so the raid fails.
	events.CarryInterrupted.Event:Connect(function(player, _model)
		stopCarrying(player, true)
	end)
end

return StealService

-- Duration type
-- by @vuppyan

local Core = require("../Core")
type Map<K, V> = Core.Map<K, V>
type Partial<T> = Core.Partial<T>

local Result = Core.Result
type Result<T, E> = Core.Result<T, E>

local fail = Core.Errors.errorWithScope("Duration")

--[=[
    A fixed-length span of time with nanosecond precision and no upper bound.

    Internally, a `Duration` is represented by two `number` fields. The first
    represents whole seconds with any sign, unbounded. The second represents a
    nanosecond adjustment in [0, 999_999_999], which is always non-negative,
    since the sign of the `Duration` lives in the seconds field. This avoids
    float64 mantissa loss, as a single `number` storing nanoseconds loses
    precision beyond ~104 days. Splitting into seconds and nanoseconds gives
    exact time arithmetic at both scales without any practical upper limit.
    Arithmetic is exact as long as the whole seconds stay below 2^53, and
    conversions to a single `number`, such as [Duration:toNanos], are subject to
    the usual float64 precision limits.

    A `Duration` may also be positive or negative infinity (see
    [Duration.INFINITE]). Infinite `Duration`s have no sub-second component, and
    operations whose result would be undefined, such as adding infinities with
    different signs or multiplying infinity by zero, throw. `NaN` is never a
    valid input.

    `Duration`s are frozen and cannot be modified.

    Supports `==`, `~=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` comparison, `tostring()`, `+`,
    `-`, `//`, and `%` arithmetic with other `Duration`s, `*` and `/` arithmetic
    with a scalar, and `-` negation.

    Error messages thrown by `Duration` functions are prefixed with the function
    that threw them, such as `[Duration.plus()]: `, after the usual position
    prefix added by `error()`. Operators report the method that backs them, so
    `a + b` reports `[Duration.plus()]`.

    @tag immutable
    @class Duration
    @since v0.1.0
]=]
local Duration = {}
Duration.__index = Duration

type DurationData = {
    read _secs: number,
    read _nanos: number,
}

export type Duration = typeof(setmetatable({} :: DurationData, Duration))

--[=[
    A set of parts in a `Duration`, returned by [Duration:toParts].

    All parts are non-negative and within their usual ranges (such as 0-23 for
    `hours`), except `days`, which is unbounded. The sign of the `Duration` is
    stored in `negative`. For infinite `Duration`s, `days` is `math.huge` and
    every other part is 0.

    [Duration.fromParts] takes a `Partial<TimeParts>` instead, where every part
    is optional and may be outside its usual range, fractional, or negative.

    @interface TimeParts
    @within Duration
    @since [UNRELEASED]
    @field negative boolean -- Whether the `Duration` is negative
    @field days number -- The whole days
    @field hours number -- The hours (0-23)
    @field minutes number -- The minutes (0-59)
    @field seconds number -- The seconds (0-59)
    @field millis number -- The milliseconds (0-999)
    @field micros number -- The microseconds (0-999)
    @field nanos number -- The nanoseconds (0-999)
]=]
export type TimeParts = {
    read negative: boolean,
    read days: number,
    read hours: number,
    read minutes: number,
    read seconds: number,
    read millis: number,
    read micros: number,
    read nanos: number,
}

--[=[
    An input set of parts in a `Duration`, used by [Duration.fromParts].

    All fields are optional, and will default to 0 (or false, in `negative`'s
    case). Parts are not limited to their usual ranges, so `{ hours = 36 }` is
    the same as `{ days = 1, hours = 12 }`, and they may be fractional or
    negative.

    @deprecated [UNRELEASED] -- Use `Partial<TimeParts>` instead

    @interface TimePartsI
    @within Duration
    @since v0.1.0
    @field negative boolean? -- Whether to negate the whole `Duration` (defaults to `false`)
    @field days number? -- The number of days (defaults to 0)
    @field hours number? -- The number of hours (defaults to 0)
    @field minutes number? -- The number of minutes (defaults to 0)
    @field seconds number? -- The number of seconds (defaults to 0)
    @field millis number? -- The number of milliseconds (defaults to 0)
    @field micros number? -- The number of microseconds (defaults to 0)
    @field nanos number? -- The number of nanoseconds (defaults to 0)
]=]
export type TimePartsI = {
    read negative: boolean?,
    read days: number?,
    read hours: number?,
    read minutes: number?,
    read seconds: number?,
    read millis: number?,
    read micros: number?,
    read nanos: number?,
}

--[=[
    An output set of parts in a `Duration`, returned by [Duration:toParts].

    All parts are non-negative and within their usual ranges (such as 0-23 for
    `hours`), except `days`, which is unbounded. The sign of the `Duration` is
    stored in `negative`. For infinite `Duration`s, `days` is `math.huge` and
    every other part is 0.

    @deprecated [UNRELEASED] -- Use `TimeParts` instead

    @interface TimePartsO
    @within Duration
    @since v0.1.0
    @field negative boolean -- Whether the `Duration` is negative
    @field days number -- The whole days
    @field hours number -- The hours (0-23)
    @field minutes number -- The minutes (0-59)
    @field seconds number -- The seconds (0-59)
    @field millis number -- The milliseconds (0-999)
    @field micros number -- The microseconds (0-999)
    @field nanos number -- The nanoseconds (0-999)
]=]
export type TimePartsO = {
    negative: boolean,
    days: number,
    hours: number,
    minutes: number,
    seconds: number,
    millis: number,
    micros: number,
    nanos: number,
}

--[=[
    A unit of time that can be used in human-readable string formatting with
    [Duration:toHumanString].

    @type HumanStringUnit "days" | "hours" | "minutes" | "seconds" | "millis"
    @within Duration
    @since v0.1.0
]=]
export type HumanStringUnit =
    "days"
    | "hours"
    | "minutes"
    | "seconds"
    | "millis"

--[=[
    Options for [Duration:toHumanString].

    @interface HumanStringOptions
    @within Duration
    @since v0.1.0
    @field maxUnits number? -- How many units to show, counting from the largest non-zero one; must be a positive integer or `math.huge` (defaults to all)
    @field smallestUnit HumanStringUnit? -- The smallest unit to show (defaults to "millis")
]=]
export type HumanStringOptions = {
    read maxUnits: number?,
    read smallestUnit: HumanStringUnit?,
}

local NANOS_MIN = 0
local NANOS_MAX = 999_999_999

-- TODO: maybe extract these to a separate time constants file where it makes sense?
local NANOS_PER_MICRO = 1_000
local NANOS_PER_MILLI = 1_000_000
local NANOS_PER_SECOND = 1_000_000_000
local SECONDS_PER_MINUTE = 60
local SECONDS_PER_HOUR = 3_600
local SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
local SECONDS_PER_WEEK = 604_800

local DATE_UNITS: { [string]: { rank: number, secs: number } } = {
    W = { rank = 1, secs = SECONDS_PER_WEEK },
    D = { rank = 2, secs = SECONDS_PER_DAY },
}
local TIME_UNITS: { [string]: { rank: number, secs: number } } = {
    H = { rank = 3, secs = SECONDS_PER_HOUR },
    M = { rank = 4, secs = SECONDS_PER_MINUTE },
    S = { rank = 5, secs = 1 },
}

local HUMAN_UNITS: { { name: HumanStringUnit, suffix: string } } = {
    { name = "days", suffix = "d" },
    { name = "hours", suffix = "h" },
    { name = "minutes", suffix = "m" },
    { name = "seconds", suffix = "s" },
    { name = "millis", suffix = "ms" },
}

local MAX_SAFE_INT = 2 ^ 53

-- Helpers that take an error `level` live in this table instead of being
-- locals: the compiler may inline local functions (at -O2), which removes
-- their stack frame and makes the level point past the real caller. Calls
-- through a table field are never inlined.
local Internal = {}

-- Helper for normalizing seconds and nanoseconds to their expected ranges.
-- `level` is the error level to blame, counted from this function.
function Internal.normalize(
    secs: number,
    nanos: number,
    level: number
): (number, number)
    if math.isinf(secs) or math.isinf(nanos) then
        if math.isinf(secs) and math.isinf(nanos) and secs ~= nanos then
            fail(
                "Cannot build a Duration from infinities with different signs",
                level,
                "new"
            )
        end
        local sign = if math.isinf(secs)
            then math.sign(secs)
            else math.sign(nanos)
        return sign * math.huge, 0
    end

    local fracSecs = secs % 1
    secs -= fracSecs
    nanos = math.round(nanos + fracSecs * NANOS_PER_SECOND)

    local carry = math.floor(nanos / NANOS_PER_SECOND)
    return secs + carry, nanos - carry * NANOS_PER_SECOND
end

local function truncateTowardZero(x: number): number
    return if x >= 0 then math.floor(x) else math.ceil(x) + 0
end

-- Splits a Duration into its sign and non-negative seconds/nanoseconds
local function toMagnitude(self: Duration): (number, number, number)
    if self._secs >= 0 then
        return 1, self._secs, self._nanos
    elseif self._nanos == 0 then
        return -1, -self._secs, 0
    end
    return -1, -self._secs - 1, NANOS_PER_SECOND - self._nanos
end

local function signedPart(sign: number, part: number): number
    return sign * part + 0 -- + 0 to handle -0
end

-- Exactly computes `n * k` for integers 0 <= n < 1e9 and k >= 0.
-- Returns (carry, rem) such that n * k == carry * 1e9 + rem, 0 <= rem < 1e9.
-- The full product can reach ~2^83 or more, so it's never formed directly.
-- Exact as long as `carry` stays below 2^53.
local function mulNanos(n: number, k: number): (number, number)
    if k >= MAX_SAFE_INT then
        -- an integer k >= 2^53 is exactly m * 2^e with an integer m < 2^53,
        -- so multiply by m exactly, then double e times with carry
        local frac, exp = math.frexp(k)
        local carry, rem = mulNanos(n, frac * MAX_SAFE_INT)
        for _ = 1, exp - 53 do
            carry *= 2
            rem *= 2
            if rem >= NANOS_PER_SECOND then
                carry += 1
                rem -= NANOS_PER_SECOND
            end
        end
        return carry, rem
    end

    -- every intermediate value below stays under 2^53
    local kHi = k // NANOS_PER_SECOND -- < 2^53 / 1e9 ~= 9.007e6
    local kLo = k - kHi * NANOS_PER_SECOND -- < 1e9

    -- n * kHi * 1e9 is exactly n * kHi whole seconds
    local carry = n * kHi -- < 1e9 * 9.007e6 ~= 9.007e15 < 2^53

    -- n * kLo can reach 1e18, so split kLo = a * 1e5 + b
    local a = kLo // 100_000 -- < 1e4
    local b = kLo - a * 100_000 -- < 1e5
    local x = n * a -- < 1e13
    local y = n * b -- < 1e14

    -- n * kLo = x * 1e5 + y, and x * 1e5 = (x // 1e4) * 1e9 + (x % 1e4) * 1e5
    carry += x // 10_000
    local rest = (x % 10_000) * 100_000 + y -- < 1e9 + 1e14
    carry += rest // NANOS_PER_SECOND
    return carry, rest % NANOS_PER_SECOND
end

-- Exactly computes (secs, nanos) * k for any finite integer k.
-- Returns unnormalized (secs, nanos), meant to be passed to Duration.new().
-- Exact as long as the resulting seconds stay below 2^53.
local function mulExact(
    secs: number,
    nanos: number,
    k: number
): (number, number)
    local sign = if k < 0 then -1 else 1
    local carry, rem = mulNanos(nanos, math.abs(k))
    -- nanos * k == sign * (carry seconds + rem nanoseconds)
    return secs * k + sign * carry, sign * rem
end

-- Exact floored division returning (q, r) where a == b * q + r where r has the
-- sign of b, and |r| < |b|. Assumes b is non-zero. `level` is the error level
-- to blame, counted from this function.
function Internal.divModFloor(
    a: Duration,
    b: Duration,
    functionName: string,
    level: number
): (number, Duration)
    -- float estimate; only off by a few for any representable quotient
    local q = math.floor(a:toSeconds() / b:toSeconds())
    if math.abs(q) >= MAX_SAFE_INT then
        fail(
            "Quotient is too large to be represented exactly",
            level,
            functionName
        )
    end

    -- exact remainder for the estimate, then step q until r is in range
    local r = a:minus(b:times(q))
    if b:isPositive() then
        -- want 0 <= r < b
        while r:isNegative() do
            q -= 1
            r = r:plus(b)
        end
        while r:compareTo(b) >= 0 do
            q += 1
            r = r:minus(b)
        end
    else
        -- want b < r <= 0
        while r:isPositive() do
            q -= 1
            r = r:plus(b)
        end
        while r:compareTo(b) <= 0 do
            q += 1
            r = r:minus(b)
        end
    end
    -- add 0 to handle -0
    return q + 0, r
end

-- Exact truncated division returning (q, r) where a == b * q + r where r has
-- the sign of a, and |r| < |b|. Assumes b is non-zero. `level` is the error
-- level to blame, counted from this function.
function Internal.divModTruncated(
    a: Duration,
    b: Duration,
    functionName: string,
    level: number
): (number, Duration)
    local q, r = Internal.divModFloor(a, b, functionName, level + 1)
    -- floor and truncation only differ when the exact quotient is negative and
    -- not whole; there's a remainder, and a and b have opposite signs
    if not r:isZero() and a:isNegative() ~= b:isNegative() then
        q += 1
        r = r:minus(b)
    end
    return q, r
end

-- `level` is the error level to blame, counted from this function, and
-- defaults to the caller's caller.
function Internal.assertDuration(
    value: any,
    operation: string,
    functionName: string,
    level: number?
): Duration
    if not Duration.is(value) then
        fail(
            `Attempted to perform {operation} on a non-Duration value: {value}`,
            level or 3,
            functionName
        )
    end
    return value :: Duration
end

-- Implementation of Duration.new(). `level` is the error level to blame,
-- counted from this function, so internal callers can blame their own caller.
function Internal.newDuration(
    secs: number,
    nanos: number,
    level: number
): Duration
    if math.isnan(secs) or math.isnan(nanos) then
        fail("Cannot create a Duration from NaN values", level, "new")
    end

    local s, n = Internal.normalize(secs, nanos, level + 1)
    return table.freeze(setmetatable({ _secs = s, _nanos = n }, Duration))
end

-- Helper for generating Duration.parse()/tryParse() error messages
local function parseErrMsg(input: string, pos: number?, reason: string): string
    return `Invalid ISO-8601 duration: "{input}" ({reason}`
        .. if pos ~= nil then ` at position {pos})` else ")"
end

--[=[
    Creates a new `Duration` from the specified number of seconds and additional
    nanoseconds.

    Fractional seconds will be split into seconds and nanoseconds. Fractional
    nanoseconds will be rounded to the nearest nanosecond, with halves rounded
    away from zero. Nanoseconds outside of [0, 999_999_999] carry into (or
    borrow from) the seconds provided, so both arguments may have any sign.

    If either argument is infinite, the result is an infinite `Duration` with
    that sign.

    ```lua
    Duration.new(1, 500_000_000) -- 1.5 seconds
    Duration.new(1, 1_500_000_000) -- 2.5 seconds, since nanoseconds carry
    Duration.new(2, -500_000_000) -- 1.5 seconds, since nanoseconds borrow
    Duration.new(1.5, 0) -- 1.5 seconds
    ```

    @since v0.1.0
    @param secs number -- The number of seconds
    @param nanos number -- The number of nanoseconds
    @return Duration -- The new `Duration`
    @error "[Duration.new()]: Cannot create a Duration from NaN values" -- Thrown if `secs` or `nanos` is `NaN`
    @error "[Duration.new()]: Cannot build a Duration from infinities with different signs" -- Thrown if `secs` and `nanos` are infinities with different signs
]=]
function Duration.new(secs: number, nanos: number): Duration
    return Internal.newDuration(secs, nanos, 3)
end

--[=[
    A duration of zero time.

    @prop ZERO Duration
    @within Duration
    @readonly
    @since v0.1.0
]=]
Duration.ZERO = Duration.new(0, 0)

--[=[
    A duration of one nanosecond.

    @prop NANOSECOND Duration
    @within Duration
    @readonly
    @since v0.1.0
]=]
Duration.NANOSECOND = Duration.new(0, 1)

--[=[
    A duration of one microsecond.

    @prop MICROSECOND Duration
    @within Duration
    @readonly

--[=[
    Creates a new `Duration` from the specified table of parts.

    Missing parts will be treated as zero, and an empty table will return a
    `Duration` of zero time. Parts may exceed their usual ranges and will carry
    over, so `{ minutes = 90 }` is the same as `{ hours = 1, minutes = 30 }`.
    Fractional parts are rounded to the nearest nanosecond.

    `negative = true` negates the sum of all parts, so negative parts with
    `negative = true` are doubly-negated and become positive.

    ```lua
    Duration.fromParts({ hours = 1, minutes = 90 }) -- 2 hours 30 minutes
    Duration.fromParts({ negative = true, minutes = 5 }) -- -5 minutes
    Duration.fromParts({ negative = true, minutes = -5 }) -- 5 minutes
    ```

    @since v0.1.0
    @param parts Partial<TimeParts> -- The table of parts
    @return Duration -- The new `Duration`
    @error "[Duration.new()]: Cannot create a Duration from NaN values" -- Thrown if any part is `NaN`, or if `days`, `hours`, `minutes`, and `seconds`, or `millis`, `micros`, and `nanos`, include infinities with different signs
    @error "[Duration.new()]: Cannot build a Duration from infinities with different signs" -- Thrown if the whole-second parts (`days` to `seconds`) and the sub-second parts (`millis` to `nanos`) are infinities with different signs
]=]
function Duration.fromParts(parts: Partial<TimeParts>): Duration
    local sign = parts.negative and -1 or 1
    local secs = sign
        * (
            (parts.days or 0) * SECONDS_PER_DAY
            + (parts.hours or 0) * SECONDS_PER_HOUR
            + (parts.minutes or 0) * SECONDS_PER_MINUTE
            + (parts.seconds or 0)
        )
    local nanos = sign
        * (
            (parts.millis or 0) * NANOS_PER_MILLI
            + (parts.micros or 0) * NANOS_PER_MICRO
            + (parts.nanos or 0)
        )
    return Internal.newDuration(secs, nanos, 3)
end
